Design reference

Building Fabricate screens

Every primitive rendered at its canonical geometry, in the shipped palette, with the API it needs to be built — then the recipes that assemble them into the four screens this app actually has.

00

How to use this

Read the foundations once. After that, work from section 13 backwards: find the screen archetype you are building, follow its recipe, and open a part's entry only when you need its API.

Every entry declares a STATUS beside its heading, and a heading naming several parts declares one per name. target means the entry is specified and the shipped component does not yet match it, or nothing ships — the specimen is what to build towards, not a description of the tree. shipped means the shipped component matches this specimen's API and geometry. divergent means a recorded decision keeps the shipped component different, and the entry names the issue that decided it. prose is a section that specifies no part. The status is FIDELITY to the specimen; how far a surface has adopted a primitive is a different question, tracked by the source-contract exemptions rather than here. Section 16 carries the divergences that are recorded inline rather than as a whole-entry verdict.

The five rules that keep screens consistent

prose
1 · One component per job

Where two surfaces do the same thing, they import the same component. If you are about to write a second version, the answer is a prop on the first.

2 · Geometry comes from the ladder

Six control heights, five radii, one 4px spacing scale. A value off the ladder is a bug, not a decision.

3 · Colour is data, not decoration

A tint identifies an entity; a semantic family reports state. Never a literal — a raw rgba() fails the colour gate.

4 · Every control declares its states

Rest, hover, focus-visible, disabled — and where they apply, readonly, invalid, loading, empty. Naming is a required prop, not an optional one.

5 · Foundry owns the window

Container queries, not viewport. Portalled popovers, not CSS offsets. No URL, no router, no toast. Section 05 is not advice.

Svelte API convention
  • Name — ariaLabel names the control, required-shaped; a member with a shipped localized fallback keeps it. ariaLabelledBy / ariaDescribedBy are id references; panelLabel / panelLabelledBy name a portalled panel. <part>Label is the text of a named part: its visible text where the part renders text, otherwise its accessible name; <part>AriaLabel only where a part needs both. label is visible text, and may also name the element that renders it.
  • Density — density, default 'default', values per specimen. size names a published ladder rung (control height or art square) and nothing else. No boolean compact as a density; a flag that changes what renders is a variant and stays.
  • Tone — tone: a member’s resting tone is its default, which a caller omits. Each member spells it as its specimen states (default, ''). The named values subtle|accent|success|info|warning|danger are shared where a member takes them. neutral is a tone only where a member’s notes name it. Each member’s notes state its own tone set, including values outside this list (positive, tag, the five kind tones).
  • Verb role — a role prop on Button, its shipped closed set neutral|primary|ghost|danger|dashed|warning, and on IconButton the closed subset neutral|primary|ghost|danger|ghost-danger (issue 2541). It is the verb role, not the ARIA attribute; no other primitive declares role, so an ARIA role reaches their root through ...rest.
  • State — busy is an action in flight on a control (focusable, aria-disabled, aria-busy); loading is a data source not yet settled.
  • Callbacks — onclick on a plain button; onChange(value) on a value control, a boolean one included; onToggle for open/closed and for flipping one item’s membership; onSelect(id) on a menu, tab strip or option list; any other event on plus its name in camelCase, as onPageChange; onChoose only on a requirement chooser.
  • Passthrough — class plus ...rest on the root, spread after class; a fixed sub-element takes <part>Props (object); a per-item hook whose value the primitive computes takes <part>DataAttr (attribute name); an attribute the primitive writes from a declared prop is passed by that prop, never through rest.
  • This list binds every component under src/ui/svelte/components/, and tests/design-system-api-convention.test.js holds it over prop names; a name kept outside it is carried in that gate’s exceptions register with its reason. Values are each specimen’s to state.

Hue drift is the widest separation between any two themes for that token. A name is a promise to the GM, who picks by the word — so a drift above 60° means the label is wrong in at least one theme.
Settled at issue 2352: the offering is a rule, not a count. A tint is pickable unless it is a NEUTRAL that would read as text or as a disabled state (bone is near-white, slate is grey) or is BOUND to a fixed brand site (ember, the Downtime companion tint). That offers ten: the original eight, then verdant and azure, appended so the eight keep their positions. Collision with a semantic colour does not disqualify a tint: verdant is byte-identical to --fab-success and azure to --fab-drop-rate-uncommon, as mist is to --fab-info, lavender to --fab-purple and butter to --fab-warning. The selected ring clears 3:1 on both added tints in all seven themes, lowest in foundry-native at 4.49:1 on verdant and 3.79:1 on azure. A stored verdant or azure is additive vocabulary with no migration: a build that predates them still draws such an essence in its tint and keeps it until the GM edits its colour, but folds such a biome onto sage and writes that back on its next save.Evidence: styles/fabricate-tokens.css declares all 13 in 7 blocks; managerColorTokens.js MANAGER_COLOR_TOKENS offers the 10, and tests/manager-color-tokens.test.js fails an offered set the rule does not produce; the only consumer of ember is WorldDowntimePreview.svelte .is-tint-ember

The drop-rate ramp

prose

Seven fixed hues, byte-identical in all seven themes. Wherever colour carries a reading it is banded: a value range maps to one of these, and the whole fill takes that colour. Nothing is interpolated, so a bar at 57% and one at 58% never land in a hue the ramp does not contain.

Type

Spectral names things. The host UI face carries interface text. JetBrains Mono carries every number a GM will compare or tune.

Mono ships 400 and 500 only
  • assets/fonts/ ships exactly jetbrains-mono-latin-400 and -500, and canon says ship only the weights the product uses.
  • Those steps would synthesize as faux-bold. Emphasis in mono comes from size and ink.
  • Every mono numeric sets tabular-nums, so 9 to 10 cannot shift the control beside it.
The UI face is host-owned
  • Canon reads it as Foundry's var(--font-body, var(--font-primary, sans-serif)), deliberately untokenized; Kicker states it itself.
  • So the ladder gives sizes, weights and roles and never names the family. A theme changing that face is a supported outcome.
  • Only serif and mono are Fabricate tokens.

Why 44 exists. The five smaller rungs cannot meet the 24×24 target minimum with real padding once a control carries a border and an icon, so the ladder needs one comfortable rung; the shipped stepper already exposes a density prop, though it selects 24px rather than a full rung. Open call for the maintainer: if you would rather solve hit targets per component through that prop than carry a sixth rung, this is the one line to delete.

These rules are cross-cutting, and are defined once here so that forty components do not each invent one.

Required on every interactive part
  • rest surface-soft · hover surface-raised · active surface-active
  • focus-visible a 2px accent ring at 2px offset — never :focus, so a mouse click does not ring

Declared where they apply
  • readonly is not disabled — it takes focus
  • invalid danger border and soft fill, plus an error message whose id the control points at
  • busy a control’s action in flight, and loading a data source not yet settled — see the rule below
The loading rule, and why it is a rule. Foundry's bundled Font Awesome kills fa-spin under prefers-reduced-motion, and every shipped spinner is aria-hidden. A busy state expressed as a spinner alone is therefore conveyed by nothing at all to a reduced-motion user. A loading control MUST set aria-busy and change its label. The spinner is decoration.Vendor rule in harvested fontawesome/css/all.min.css (.fa-spin under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) · ArmedDangerButton.svelte · Button.svelte

Hit targets, naming, announcement

prose
24×24 minimum
The hit area may exceed the painted area. A 2px divider still gets a 24px handle; a bare × is 24px around a 9px glyph.
Naming
  • Any control whose visible text is a glyph or a number takes its accessible name as a required prop.
  • A name composed from a value — “increase quantity to 3” — is derived by a shared helper, because 23 call sites drifted the last time it was not.
Announcement
  • A change with no visible focus consequence is announced. Reorder says “Moved {name} to position {n} of {total}”.
  • Order matters: move focus first, then announce — polite speech is cancelled by a focus change.
Motion
  • 140ms ease for a control state change, read from --fab-motion-control, which the sheet’s :root declares once. Nothing else animates, and no keyframes ship. Shipped at issue 1523 (decision D2): tests/components/motion-token-gate.test.js fails a literal time or timing on a transition or animation in the sheet or any Svelte scoped block.
  • Under reduced motion every transition MUST be removed. Shipped at issue 1523: the sheet’s one prefers-reduced-motion: reduce block sets transition: none !important on .fabricate, the chat cards, their dice tiles and the canvas prompt and everything inside them, no component writes a block of its own, and the same gate fails a scoped or second block.
The minimum is 24×24, and the hit area may exceed the paint. Two shipped components cite WCAG 2.2 §2.5.8 by name as the reason they carry a density prop at all, so a control that cannot meet it in a dense row offers a comfortable density its caller selects.stepperLabels.js (1050) · listReorderAnnouncement.js (1311) · announceAfterFocus.js (1157) · ui-visual-style/spec.md §Shared product UI primitives
05

Foundry contract

Everything here renders inside Foundry's CSS, inside its event handling, inside a window it owns. Six constraints bind the whole set — none of them optional.

Keyboard escape

Foundry recognises focus only in form controls, contentEditable, or a button with a form. Any other focusable element handling arrows, Page or Home/End MUST carry data-keyboard-focus="true", or the keypress also pans or zooms the canvas. Space on a bare button pauses the game for the whole table.

Listbox focus model

A popover KEEPS DOM focus in its search input — or in its trigger, where the search field is suppressed — and drives selection with aria-activedescendant. Roving focus onto option buttons is forbidden — it re-arms the canvas bindings. Shipped: the option rows stayed buttons, took tabindex="-1" and data-keyboard-focus="true", and never receive focus.

Floating surfaces portal

The manager root and its scrolling panels each clip, so an absolutely-positioned panel cannot escape them by CSS. Portalling escapes those; it does not escape core's own .window-content, which is the box the panel is then clamped inside. Portal to the application root — .fabricate-manager or .fabricate-app — never document.body, which loses window stacking — then measure, flip and clamp.

Core CSS collisions

Core's V1 resets do not protect V2 apps. Every button sets its own height and min-height; every input its own width; radio and checkbox need their pseudo-elements removed as well as appearance:none; and the serif ladder must name the element it renders on, because bare headings take core's colour and margins.

Transient feedback is core's

ui.notifications owns it — 83 call sites and a progress-handle API — and core renders its toasts over the module window anyway. Fabricate ships no toast. Destructive confirmation defaults to confirmDialog; the arm-then-confirm pattern is a carve-out for high-frequency row actions and for bulk actions that state impact in-panel.

There is no URL

Foundry's client is a single page with no router. Page state, filter state and navigation live in an app-level store. An in-app href either does nothing or navigates the game away and disconnects the client. Every breakpoint is an @container query, and a container query adds no specificity — so declare the narrow case after the wide one.

  • group 1px border · radius 7 · surface-soft · 2px padding and gap · 28px by default, 30px at comfortable density
  • adjunct 22×22 by default, 24×24 at comfortable density · icon 9px · hover surface-raised on a 6px corner

  • disabled the group at opacity .45, both adjuncts text-disabled
  • adjuncts declare data-keyboard-focus="true", because a button outside a form is otherwise invisible to Foundry's focus test
  • composite as the duration editor ships it: one card per unit, years, months, days, hours and minutes, in five equal columns 8px apart; each card a 1px border, radius 9, --fab-surface-soft and 8px padding, its uppercase label at 0.58rem 700 with .08em tracking above a vertical stepper whose adjuncts are 26px and whose input is 30px at 1.05rem; a vertical stepper fills its slot (drawn in a 48px slot), borderless and transparent, its glyph 11px
  • null endpoint its label reads --fab-text-muted at rest; horizontal and unfilled, its input is at least 64px wide and never narrower than the label; its decrement is disabled
  • The kit draws every icon as a stroked sprite, so the adjunct glyphs here are lighter and narrower than the shipped Font Awesome solid ones; the glyph’s box and its centring are the spec, and the stroke weight is the kit’s stand-in, shared by every entry.
  • The composite’s unit labels are drawn in --fab-text-muted; the shipped --fab-text-subtle measures 3.36–3.88:1 at 9px, debt owned by issue 2368.
Svelte API
  • value number | null · onChange (value) required — a refused typed value is replaced by value when the input loses focus
  • min · max · step
  • allowUnset — clearing commits null; adjuncts step from min ?? 0
  • ariaLabel · decrementLabel · incrementLabel required, derived
  • orientation horizontal | vertical
  • density default | comfortable
  • fill · placeholder · inputProps · disabled
  • formatValue · parseValue · stops · nullLabel — the opt-in formatted mode: a role="spinbutton" text input with decimal inputmode that commits on Enter or blur, restores its display for invalid text or on Escape, and steps to the nearest stop above or below, so an off-list value stays exact until stepped. nullLabel names an endpoint one step below the lowest stop, which carries no aria-valuenow; without one, null is unset and renders the placeholder
  • A unit is not a prop: a caller renders it beside the group. The unset placeholder inks --fab-text-muted from the component’s own ::placeholder rule while the input is not keyboard-focused, and clears 4.5:1 on its well in all seven themes (issue 2358); the unset value drawn here takes the same ink.
The value is always editable. A click-only stepper is a documented keyboard regression, which is why the shipped component states the rule in its own docblock. <Button> <IconButton>

Button · shippedIconButton · shipped

One component, six roles, three heights. Each role names a VERB, not a colour: neutral is the secondary verb and the default, primary the leading verb of its cluster — create or commit in a chrome cluster, and in an inspector rail the verb that opens the selected record — at most one per cluster, ghost the quiet verb that changes no record — Back, Open, View, Copy — and never its cluster’s leading verb, dashed the append verb at the foot of the list it adds to, danger the destructive verb, and warning the caution verb, which proceeds against a flagged rule or breaks a re-makeable reference, and destroys nothing.

Issue 1648 IconButton extension. The rung size="24" (issue 2541 named it as a string, as Button’s rungs are) opts into a 24px-square border-box, 24px minimum dimensions, zero padding and fixed 24px flex-basis, retaining the existing 6px radius and the caller’s role. The default size="" preserves the existing default/pager geometry.
Ruled: PRIMARY is the SUCCESS family, everywhere. Maintainer, 2026-09-03. The specimen CSS above already paints .k-btn.primary with --fab-success, and the shipped sheet agrees — .fabricate-button.is-primary:not(:disabled) sets background: var(--fab-success) with the matching border and ink. There is no second accent for a commit verb. ui-visual-style/spec.md’s “Right-inspector actions” rule stated an accent for that stack; issue 1521 amended it and folded the inspector action button into this primitive, and the row is recorded in section 16.
Settled (maintainer ruling 2026-10-20, issue 2557): the button takes href and tag="a" for an external destination, drawn as a button, with target and rel beside them; the in-app prohibition in design-system/spec.md stands, because there is no router. The Svelte API above draws that reading, a caller rule rather than a component guard, and section 16 records it settled.
The dashed adder is a role, not a component. It is one of six closed roles on the button that owns the meaning, and canon prefers extending that primitive over introducing a second one that owns half of it. fullWidth is a prop rather than a role, because spanning the container is a statement about the container and not about the verb.ui-visual-style/spec.md §Shared product UI primitives · Button.svelte classes
The icon-only half ships as its own component, at the specimen’s geometry and with a closed role set (issue 2541). It was extracted from 82 hand-rolled manager-icon-button sites (a class issue 1507 retired) across 37 components; a census walking each component’s Svelte AST found ONE element host, so it takes no polymorphism prop. Geometry: the shipped control is 34×34, and 28 only inside .fabricate-pagination — and since issue 2541 the icon 34 above draws it, the specimen having yielded to the shipped pixel under the maintainer’s 2026-09-18 ruling, with the pager’s 28 drawn as the .s28 rung. And the shipped radius is 9, the band of its 34px height since issue 1523 put every corner on its size band, except inside .fabricate-pagination, where issue 1504 moved the pager’s buttons onto this specimen’s 7 (.k-btn.icon.s28 since issue 2541) so the pager’s arrows read as one matched set. So there are now two shipped radii as well as two shipped sizes, and the SIZE records are unchanged by that change: only the pager’s corner moved. Roles: since issue 2541 it takes a role prop, the closed set neutral|primary|ghost|danger|ghost-danger, mapped by a named ROLE_CLASSES to the is-* classes the sheet already paints, ghost-danger being the compound the sheet declares by name; states (is-locked, is-roll-needed) stay pass-through class, and every call site names its role and glyph through role and icon, the swept sites’ class sets unchanged. Name: it shows its accessible name as a plain-text tooltip under the pointer and keyboard focus alike, no call site writes a native title, and the three information-bearing hints pass tooltip. The bare × above is role="ghost" at the 24 rung — the ghost’s transparent, borderless paint at the rung’s 24px box, the journal history’s dismiss — and the icon 24 unit draws the same rung neutral and bordered. Both button families are now rooted at a class the primitive emits, and each declares its own focus ring. Issue 1502, measured with this commit. Button emits fabricate-button and IconButton emits fabricate-icon-button, each as the FIRST literal of its own classes array, and every rule in the two families that used to read .fabricate-manager .manager-button… (a class issue 1507 retired) is now a COMPOUND on that root at unchanged specificity — one class for one class, declaration blocks byte-identical. 81 of Button’s 109 sheet selectors and 16 of IconButton’s 22 moved; the rest name a caller’s own container in their ancestor chain — or, for one per-view override each, an application root qualified by an attribute — and are exempt. Ring: each family declares the PAIR itself — outline: none; box-shadow: none on :focus, then outline: 2px solid var(--fab-accent) with a 2px offset on :focus-visible — because both halves of the module’s focus chrome are bare-element selectors the module root .fabricate declares for every application (issue 1501), and a control rooted at the primitive can no longer assume it is inside a Fabricate root at all. Without the strip half, Foundry core’s a.button:focus, button:focus orange outline and 4px glow (foundry2.css) survive UNDER the accent ring in a host carrying no Fabricate root class. Bare-element chrome: the family declares font: inherit on a rule of its own, rooted at the family root ALONE so the baseline is a FLOOR rather than an override — enough to beat the user agent’s button font in a host that declares nothing, and deliberately not enough to beat a caller’s per-site rule on a pass-through class. Written at the family’s own compound specificity it TIED those rules and won on source order, which deleted the recipe row’s 0.68rem lock and pencil. The block that declares line-height: 1 is the more specific of the two, so the shorthand never reaches it. Keyboard: both emit data-keyboard-focus="true", so Foundry’s KeyboardManager#hasFocus stops returning false for a button outside a form — a real behaviour change, and the first bite out of the 278-element formless-button debt below (now 277). shipped

The inline two-step destructive control for a high-frequency row action, or a bulk action that states its impact in the panel: the first press arms, the second confirms. It is a caller of <Button> at role="danger", never a seventh role. It is a member rather than a composition because the arm-then-confirm machine — the token, the face it holds and the disarms it reports — is behaviour no other member owns; <RunActionBar>’s armed cancel, with its keep button and prompt, is a different control.

Canonical spec
  • idle the danger role at the button’s rung: 34 in the body, 38 at size="38" beside the page header’s actions; glyph idleIcon, trash by default, and idleIcon="" drops it
  • armed --fab-danger fill, --fab-on-danger ink; the glyph swaps and no caller may suppress it
  • busy Button’s busy face over the danger role: opacity .7, cursor: progress, no hover, never the armed fill, so it keeps the role’s resting paint at its site — the danger outline on --fab-surface-soft where no site restates it, and the soft-red fill only in a bulk panel’s dock, which is that dock’s own site form; the spinner is decoration and busyLabel is the signal; the shipped default glyph is the spinner and the specimen draws the clock, so its lab row passes busyIcon. Why aria-disabled, not disabled: disabling a focused button fires blur in Chromium and Firefox and drops the keyboard to the page, and a blur while busy never disarms the control

  • keyboard Escape and blur each disarm only while armed and not busy, and the Escape that disarms does not reach Foundry; Button writes data-keyboard-focus

The bare · no well specimen above ships as tone, not as well. That specimen is drawn with the exact two options the requirement row's tag-match control carries, and the shipped answer for it is a value on a tone prop rather than a well boolean — because the well is not the only thing that goes. The track is edged and the chosen segment lit in the TAG family, matching the requirement row's own border, its tag chips and its + Tag pill; a boolean that only removed the well would still have left the one control that is about tags painted in the neutral warm family (issue 1373). It is distinct from the per-option variant ramp on the same component: variant tints one ACTIVE segment to say what CHOOSING it means, and tone says what the whole track is ABOUT. It carries the track's scale as well as its colour, so a caller passes no density beside it — and the scale is load-bearing rather than cosmetic, because this control is the only thing a tag requirement row carries that the other three kinds do not, and a taller track raises every tag row above its siblings. <Segmented> takes already-localized labels (issue 2588). An option’s label is the string itself, where it was a labelKey and a fallback, and SegmentedControl resolves no lang key, so its import closure holds no module outside its own file and the published-component seam can take it; each caller resolves its key where it builds the options, and an untranslated key still renders the caller’s English fallback. RadioCardGroup takes final display text too (issue 2601), which its callers resolve with localizeOptions; EditorTabs takes final display text too (issue 2601), which its callers resolve with localizeTabs. No rendered text, title or accessible name changes. SegmentedControl is published through game.fabricate.api.ui (issue 2644).

Every select in the app renders this list, with one structural exception stated below. A native <select> popup is drawn by the operating system, so it ignores the theme, differs between browsers and platforms, and cannot carry a tick, a group heading, a description, a badge or a reason for being unavailable. One control everywhere is what makes a select look the same on every machine.

The selected tick is configurable: it earns its column where options are close cousins and a reader needs to confirm which is live, and is dropped where the trigger already states the value and the list is short. It is a property of the list, not of the option.

The one exception. A select inside a Foundry-owned dialog body stays native: DialogV2 cleans its content and re-serialises it through innerHTML, so no mounted component survives, its callers read values back through form.elements, and its <dialog> has no application root to portal into. The selects inside DialogV2 bodies are the ONE structural exception. No component is exempt by a reason of its own — this entry used to say two were, and that precedence was withdrawn in spec.md before issue 1504 converted the first of them. Every remaining native select is DEBT that the ratchet compares with the base commit: a change may not add one unless the element carries a <!-- ratchet-exempt(design-system): reason --> marker, and converting one is reported and never required. The remaining ones are the manager’s, and issue 1777 owns them.
inline 30 — a field that is one cell of a row
Oak Haft
A row is an editable record in a list. The field drops to 30px and takes a bg-2 fill to read as nested inside the row's bg-1.

The shell shipped first; the CONTROL shipped at issue 1504. Field.svelte is the labelled column this entry describes as “part of the primitive, not something each screen re-invents” — a flex-direction: column box holding a kicker caption, the control and its hint — and 81 call sites across 23 components render it. The 38px control shell above it, the option list, the value/onChange/options API and the configurable tick now ship too, as components/Select.svelte, composed over SearchablePopover with the query field suppressed. <Search> shipped last, at issue 1782, so all three names and the block itself now read shipped.

A THIRD SIZE RUNG, and its reason. toolbar — 34 / radius 9 / 11.5px / weight 600 / fill --fab-bg-1 — is not in the Canonical spec above because this entry was written before the scoped catalogue existed. That toolbar is a shipped 34px control line whose search field, direction toggle and segmented control this change does not move, so a converted sort key on the 38px form rung would have stood four pixels proud of its own row. 34, 9, 11.5 and 600 are all published ladder and ramp values, so the rung costs no debt. Its TYPE is written as a literal rather than as var(--fab-manager-recipe-control-font), because that property is declared only under .fabricate-manager and a primitive rooted outside every application may not read one — outside the area it is undefined and the declaration falls back to inheritance. Its WEIGHT is the 600 the sort-direction Button computes on the recipes, components and essences browser rows, measured in Chromium (issue 2257 D8; the maintainer kept the rung at 34, 2026-10-07).

Six divergences from this entry’s surface, each with its reason. The FILL is stated per size as a token, because this entry’s own “surface-soft in cards · bg-2 inside bg-1 rows” is CONTEXTUAL and not one of the three shipped call sites is either context. A call site may state its own trigger fill and its own width floor as a descendant rule from its wrapper class — a divergence from this entry’s prop-only surface, taken because the trigger’s box belongs to the row it sits in and six of the seven pagers wanted a different one until the pager left Select for a segmented control at issue 2546. id and name are satisfied by an aria-labelledby from the trigger to the caption the labelled form renders, rather than by a for/id pair, because there is no labelable element carrying an id for a for to point at. It was a <Field as="label"> CONTAINMENT until issue 1510 — the containment named the trigger perfectly well, a <button> being labelable, and the earlier claim that it does not was corrected at issue 1511 — but a <label> also FORWARDS a caption click into the control it names, and this control’s panel is dismissed on mousedown while it is open, so from the open state the caption dismissed the list and the forwarded click re-opened it. The host is <Field as="div"> now and the pointer is the whole mechanism; name is emitted on that button, valid and inert. minWidth/maxWidth are declared per size because the shared panel’s 240px default is wider than a short numeric list AND is floored by a sheet rule the primitive has to override. The option shape carries a disabled? this entry does not list, beside the disabledReason? it does. And triggerProps is part of the declared surface because the converted call sites drive their control by a data-* hook that a registry step, the mounted suites and the Foundry smoke all address. It is NOT enough for a native tooltip: SearchablePopover spreads it first and then writes title, aria-label and aria-labelledby from its own props, so any of the three placed in triggerProps is deleted. Issue 1510 added a triggerTitle pass-through for the first of them, and an ariaDescribedBy beside the two name props for the DESCRIPTION the labelled form draws and nothing announced — its hint or error span now carries an id the trigger points at, and a caller drawing its own conditional hint passes the id it drew. Together they take the declared surface to 25 props.

Declared with no caller on this commit, and held by test rather than by a frame: mono, icon, error, readonly, and the option shape’s badge and disabledReason. Issue 1510’s second phase gave triggerTitle its two callers in the recipe studio, and placeholder, invalid and the option shape’s disabled their one at the checks trigger editor’s tier-step target. This register is CORRECTED as well as shortened, and it separates the component props from the option shape’s fields, because the two disableds are different declarations. The prop label lost its no-caller status at the twelve interactables call sites (issue 1520) and the prop disabled at InteractableConfigRoot.svelte (issue 1520) and the manager’s BulkEditSelect.svelte (issue 1504), without this sentence moving; issue 1510 gives hint its first caller at the world currency provider field. The phase that writes this re-reads the register against the tree rather than predicting it.

The shipped prop is a HOST, and the set is closed. as takes label, div or fieldset, with no default and no fourth member. Measured across the corpus the convention it replaced used all three — 56 label, 31 div, 1 fieldset — and the difference is an accessible name rather than a treatment: a label field names the control it wraps and a div field must not, because 31 of those sites hold two controls, none, or one already named elsewhere. A missing or unrecognised value renders the inert div and warns, because label and fieldset both carry behaviour and neither may be reached by omission. class is APPENDED to fabricate-field, never a replacement, and every other attribute passes through.Field.svelte — 81 callers · ui-visual-style/spec.md §Shared product UI primitives
Field is now rooted at the class it emits, and it declares its own floor, its own element chrome and its own focus pair. Issue 1508, measured with this commit, and about the Field name in this heading ONLY — Search and Select each carry their own entry. Field.svelte writes fabricate-field as the first literal of its own class array. Of the family’s 27 sheet selectors, 9 are owned and re-rooted as compounds on that class, three more are caller-CLASS compounds that share a selector list with owned members and moved with them, and the remaining 15 name a caller’s own container — or, for two, an application root qualified by a view attribute — and are exempt. Floor: the root is a WRAPPER and the control is a bare input, select or textarea, so the floor is written at the family root PLUS the element it owns, (0,1,1), rather than at the root alone. It declares font: inherit and nothing else, because at (0,1,1) it TIES the manager’s own bare-element baseline rather than losing to it and any further declaration would be a real move inside the manager; and it is positioned immediately below that baseline, because font is a shorthand and .fabricate-manager textarea { line-height: 1.4 } and the @supports (appearance: base-select) select rule restate a font longhand at the same rank further down. Element chrome is a SEPARATE rule restating the area’s element-TYPED predicate leg for leg — appearance, -webkit-appearance and min-height: 34px over the six text-entry types and textarea — because folded into the floor over :is(input, select, textarea) the same two declarations would reach the radios, ranges, steppers and selects that predicate deliberately excludes. Ring: a PAIR, the strip as one :is(input, textarea):focus member declared above a repaint of two comma-separated legs. select is excluded from both halves deliberately: it was written when a select leg at (0,2,1) would have tied .fabricate-app select:focus-visible and won on source order, deleting the inset ring that existed because an outset outline on a select is clipped — and that rule was deleted at issue 1511 with the player app’s last native select, so the exclusion now stands on the narrower ground that the only selects a field can host are the manager’s remaining native ones, which take the module ring until they convert at issue 1777. Status does not move: the re-root alters neither this entry’s API nor its geometry.Field.svelte · styles/fabricate-manager-shell.css .fabricate-field :is(input, textarea) · styles/fabricate-manager-library.css .fabricate-field textarea (element chrome), .fabricate-field :is(input, textarea):focus, .fabricate-field input:focus-visible, .fabricate-field textarea:focus-visible · 27 family selectors, 9 owned · re-rooted-controls-host-independence.test.js
The Field caption is the kicker, drawn by the primitive, and its box carries the form rung’s value type. Issue 2532 moved the caption onto the primitive and the box onto the form rung’s 500 12.5px. The first-child span of a fabricate-field now takes the kicker’s 700 8.5px, .11em tracking, upper case and muted ink from a family rule below a caller’s own caption class, and a text control inside the box reads 12.5px at weight 500 through the family floor, where the box used to set 0.82rem at 700 for both. The caption is not the Kicker primitive, which takes no id and cannot be an aria-labelledby target. Status does not move.Field.svelte · fabricate.css

A field whose parent is a flex column adds flex: none at its call site; the column-parent variant that would absorb it is recorded in section 16.
The search field is built at the specimen (issue 1782, maintainer ruling 2). Every non-compact search — 30 call sites, the eight player searches and the journal’s among them — is the 38 / radius 9 / --fab-surface-soft shell with its glyph in flow, and the four density="compact" sites keep their shipped box as a ruled exception. The size prop and the is-size-38 field rule fold into the default, and every site rule that re-sized or re-boxed the field is deleted; tests/components/search-field-geometry-gate.test.js fails a new one. <Typeahead>

shipped

A query field that commits a choice. Typing narrows a suggestion list hung beneath the field, and each pick is written at once — into a single slot, a filter, or one more id on a short list the screen already draws. It owns no token run, no bound and no staging, which is what tells it from a set picker; a field that only narrows a list on screen is a search.

open — the second suggestion active from the keyboard, the first under the pointer
brew
Brew Potion of Healing

The field keeps DOM focus throughout; the active suggestion is named by aria-activedescendant and drawn by its outline, and no suggestion is a tab stop. The list floats over the page beneath the field’s shell, at least as wide, and flips above it only where the window has no room below.
what a pick writes — the caller’s own list, beside the field
Search recipes…
Brew Greater Healing
The chips are the caller’s markup, not the typeahead’s: it renders no token run and states no count, and the caller decides whether a pick also clears the query.

<RunActionBar>

shipped

The controls above a run in flight. Four things a player can do to a run — act on this stage, hold it, set how it finishes, abandon it — in one fixed order at one height, so any two runs are operated the same way.

ready — the primary is live
Order is fixed left to right: cancel, hold, completion, act. The primary is the only filled control; every sibling is a bordered secondary. Every button sits at 34 / radius 9 — the call to action is carried by fill and ink, never by being taller, because a run that is merely waiting would otherwise shrink its own bar and move every control beside it (the completion switch is the one recorded 2px exception).
counting down — nothing to press, and the completion switch appears
Complete
Not actionable is disabled and never aria-busy: nothing is pending, the clock simply has not reached it. The primary keeps its position and states the wait rather than vanishing. The completion switch is offered only while the run counts down — a stage whose time is up is the player’s to finish, and a stage carrying a check can never be handed over, because the roll is what ends it. The switch is SegmentedControl’s well rather than a control height: 26px segments in a 4px well with a 1px edge, 36 overall, so a counting-down bar stands 2px taller.
paused — Resume is the action
The primary is dropped, not disabled. A second dead button reading “Paused” beside Resume says the same thing twice. The completion switch goes too: a paused run serves no time, so there is nothing for it to govern.
a stage waiting on a choice — the primary says which
Pause is disabled with a reason on hover — a run waiting on the player is not counting down, so there is no time to hold. The blocker is stated once, beneath the progress kicker, and the primary names its kind rather than repeating the sentence.
cancel armed — the siblings step aside

Closes the run at stage 2; what earlier stages spent stays spent.

Arm-then-confirm rather than confirmDialog: this is the high-frequency case the routing table carves out, and the confirm can state its own impact — “closes the run at stage 2; what earlier stages spent stays spent” — which a generic dialog cannot. While it is armed it is the only decision on the row, so pause, the switch and the primary are all withdrawn rather than left competing with it. The decision sits at the far right of the line, as begin’s does, and its prompt is a full-width callout beneath it (issue 1648, M16 and M26), so a longer translation never moves the buttons.
Canonical spec
  • height every button 34 · radius 9 · gap --fab-space-2, the icon-only cancel included
  • order cancel · pause/resume · completion switch · primary
  • primary the one filled control — --fab-success on --fab-on-accent
  • switch a kicker plus SegmentedControl’s well: 26px segments in a 4px well with a 1px edge, 36 overall — geometry only; ground and ink are Segmented’s, recorded on its own entry — not a toggle: neither value is “off”
  • cancel icon-only, so its accessible name names the run
  • disabled for a control the clock has not reached; aria-busy for none of them
Svelte API
  • Read from RunActionBar.svelte’s $props() at issue 1644.
  • run the run record — the bar reads its id, which keys armed, its paused or pauseState, which puts Resume in Pause’s place, and its busy
  • runLabel required — the icon-only cancel and the switch group both name the run when their own labels are absent
  • primary {label, icon, enabled, reason, title, busy, busyLabel} required · onPrimary
  • begin null | {label, icon, enabled, reason, prompt, busyLabel} · onBegin — at an unstarted stage it takes the primary’s place, and its prompt is a full-width callout beneath the row
  • pause {label, icon, enabled, reason, title, ariaLabel} · onPause · resume {label, icon, disabled, title, ariaLabel} · onResume
  • cancel {icon, ariaLabel, title, disabled, confirmLabel, keepLabel, prompt} · onCancel, called by the armed confirm
  • completion false | {label, options, value, onChange, groupName, ariaLabel} — omit and the switch is not rendered
  • armed bindable — local to the bar, reset when run.id changes
  • Every callback defaults to a no-op, and there is no rest spread.
Why the completion switch is a segmented and not a toggle. Section 14 routes a value that could be “none” to a toggle and a one-of-N scope to a segmented. Both settings here are live behaviour a player is choosing between — by hand is not the absence of as time passes — and each needs its own icon and its own hover sentence, which a toggle has nowhere to put. It is one setting for the whole run, not per stage, because a player sets an intention once and does not want to re-declare it at every stage.
One thing this bar must never grow. A world-clock control. The clock is the GM’s; the player window states it and never moves it. A run set to finish on its own resolves on the tick the clock lands on, and carries a bolt on its list row so the player can see which runs will move without them.
Measured at issue 1644; shipped at issue 2257. On its override frames ready-single, cancel-confirmation and paused, and on waiting-auto-eligible for the switch, the canonical spec holds: every button at 34 and radius 9 with a gap of 8, the fixed order, the 34×34 icon-only cancel, the success-filled primary on --fab-on-accent, the warning-family Resume, and a disabled, never busy, primary while the clock runs. A recorded deviation: the switch is SegmentedControl’s well, 26px segments in a 4px well with a 1px edge, so it measures 36 and a counting-down bar stands 2px taller than one without it, an accepted deviation from the “bar never changes height” rule above, not a debt: the shipped well is SegmentedControl’s, and a 34 well would need 24px segments; the specimen draws that well (issue 2257 D22). Its completion kicker is the shipped <Kicker> since issue 2257, because the hand-rolled subtle ink measured under the 4.5:1 floor. The armed cancel sets its prompt as a callout beneath a right-aligned decision, the layout ruled at issue 1648 (M16 and M26), and the specimen above draws it. The neutral controls’ weight and ink and the danger confirm’s ground are <Button>’s, recorded against its own entry.

Canonical spec
  • track 46 · radius 9 · bg-0 · 1px border — fixed, never content-dependent
  • handle 24×24 hit area, col-resize, over a 2×16 grip at radius 1 in --fab-text-secondary at full opacity, which clears 3:1 on every band fill in every palette; it lights --fab-accent on hover or drag unless the strip is disabled
  • ticks one under each divider in the .k-count type, mono 10.5px, --fab-space-2xs under the track; a leading tick only when the caller passes one
  • markers a fixed marker is a 1px full-height line in solid --fab-text-muted; a draggable marker is a 9px --fab-accent dot straddling the track’s top edge in a 13px lane, over a 24×24 hit area that ends 11px into the track, clear of every divider
  • rail a 24px row under the track, one 24×24 “+” per band at least two steps wide, centred on the value it seeds
  • keyboard role="slider", arrows / Page / Home / End — and data-keyboard-focus="true"; a read-only strip has no handle to reach

  • rules spans tile · min span enforced · ends clamp
Svelte API
  • domain [min, max]
  • spans {id, label, from, to, colour, ink, index}[]
  • onChange (patch) required
  • binding relative | fixed | simple | start — start writes {binding, index, start}, the start of the band beginning at the divider; unlike the other bindings it may draw a single band
  • onChange and onMarkerChange take {phase} second: a pointer move emits drag, its release or cancel re-emits the last patch as commit, and every key emits commit
  • readonly — a derived band picture: no handles, and the group aria-describedby a visually hidden list of each band's name and caller-formatted range
  • leadingTick string — a label under the track's start, before the boundary ticks; a count strip passes <0 under its Botch band
  • markers {id, value, label, valueText?, draggable?, snap?: step | band}[] · onMarkerChange ({id, value, index}, {phase})
  • addable · railLabel · addLabel(band) · onAdd ({index, value}) — the value is the band’s midpoint rounded down to the step, and the strip creates nothing
  • axis is formatValue(value) for every tick and value text, with min/max and ticks (default on); rangeSublabels draws each band’s range under its name; minSpan is step
Shipped: the check editors and Gathering’s time-of-day bar draw this strip, at 46 / r9 / bg-0. Issue 2431 gives the shipped strip its markers, its add rail, the start binding and range sublabels, all opt-in, and the Times of day panel adopts it in that issue’s second change, retiring Gathering’s 50 / r8 / bg-1 strip. Those values were measured from the prototype and pinned by a parity fixture; the earlier 44 / 8 / raised-surface values were chosen rather than measured — a translucent raised surface let whatever the strip was stacked on show through an unfilled gap.

The height is fixed and never grows with content: a strip whose height varies shoves the caller’s steppers down the page, so a sublabel fits inside 46, and a draggable marker’s lane sits above the track rather than in it. It ships the specimen’s handle at issue 2435: the 2×16 grip, its radius 1 the pill its 2px width makes, under a col-resize cursor, in --fab-text-secondary at full opacity where this drawing once drew --fab-text at .35, which measured 2.2–2.8:1 on the band tints in every palette, under the 3:1 non-text floor; it lights --fab-accent on hover or drag unless the strip is disabled, a state this drawing does not draw.   • empty 1px dashed border-strong on surface-soft · a centred stack, 4px apart: an 18px glyph in text-subtle, the title at 12px / 600 in text-secondary, the hint in text-muted
  • linked 1px solid border-strong on bg-1 · the icon chip at its 38 rung, drawing the document’s image where it has one · name serif 600 14px under the same two-line cap · beneath the name, in order: the uuid in mono 10px where the caller asks for it or the value has no name, the hint, the subline, each only where passed · copy over unlink, each the icon button, in a column 4px apart
  • missing 1px solid danger-border on danger-soft · the chip draws the alert glyph in danger-text, never the document’s image or the caller’s glyph, because a broken link must not look like a working one; in foundry-native, where danger-text equals body text, the name’s ink matches a linked name’s, so the hint or subline carries the state in words and the alert glyph’s shape adds it for sight, the chip being decorative · the name in danger-text · where the value has no name, its uuid line stands in the name’s place in the uuid’s own size and ink, and the hint or subline carries the state · never silently blanks: the stored uuid and the hint stay visible · stays a drop target, so a dropped document replaces the missing one · Relink, the button, then copy, then unlink, in one column in that order, each only where the caller passes its handler
  • compact a prompt beside a record already shown in full, never a summary: the caller’s glyph over a title of one line over a note of one line, centred, on a 1px dashed border-strong hairline at radius 9, with no ground, no floor, no tile behind the glyph, no uuid and no action · a caller whose note would wrap shortens it · it draws neither the linked nor the missing face, whatever value and state hold
  • ink the uuid, the hint and the subline are text-muted on the linked ground and text-secondary on the missing ground, because text-muted computes to 4.32:1 on danger-soft over bg-2 in the default theme, under the 4.5:1 floor · the empty hint and both compact lines are text-muted · text-subtle computes to about 3.7:1 on bg-1 in the default theme, also under it · the empty and compact glyphs alone are text-subtle
  • disabled refuses a drop, draws no dragover face, dims to 0.55 in every state, and disables its copy, unlink and relink actions
  • keyboard the zone is not a tab stop and has no key path of its own: a caller whose document can be chosen from a list offers that list beside the zone or in its place · the actions are buttons in tab order, in drawn order
  • names the zone is a group named by its title, the document’s name, or its uuid where the value has no name · the chip is decorative · each action’s label names what it does · missing is carried by the hint’s or the subline’s text as well as by colour, which the group names as its description, so a caller passes one in missing
Svelte API
  • value {uuid, name, img} | null — a uuid, not an id; null, or a value with neither uuid nor name, is empty; a value with no name draws its uuid line in the name’s place
  • documentType Item | Macro | Scene | … — matched against data.type
  • state empty | linked | missing — empty is a record with no linked document, the manager’s “none”; missing is a stored uuid that no longer resolves; unlink is the action that returns a linked zone to empty. Unset, it is empty for a null value and linked otherwise; the caller passes missing, because only the caller resolves the document. A null value, or empty itself, draws empty whatever else is passed, and compact draws neither linked nor missing
  • title · hint · subline — the prompt’s title, which a linked zone replaces with the document’s name; the line under it, which says what a drop does; and a second line; each drawn only where passed · emptyIcon the glyph the prompt draws and a linked chip falls back to, 18px in empty, 13px in compact, and the chip’s own glyph size where the chip falls back to it
  • showUuid draws the uuid line in linked; missing, and a value with no name, draw it always
  • onDrop (data) — the raw drag data, after the type and uuid guard · onUnlink · onCopy · onRelink — each action renders only where its handler is passed; copy puts the uuid on the clipboard; relink renders in missing alone, and never on a drag-only source
  • copyLabel · unlinkLabel the two icon actions’ accessible names · relinkLabel the Relink button’s text
  • compact the prompt form · disabled
  • Passthrough: kind the per-site id on data-item-drop-zone · hookAttrs a bag of attributes over the closed region set root, hint, copy and unlink · unlinkDataAttr one attribute name on the unlink action
Match on data.type, store a uuid. The drop discriminator is the document name Foundry puts in data.type. The drop path RESOLVES the payload rather than reading data.uuid directly. On Foundry 13 and 14 every core document drag, from a directory or a compendium, carries a uuid; resolveDropUuid also reads the legacy {pack, id} shape a third-party drag source may build, so the call site never needs to know which arrived. A bare id is unresolvable without its collection, so the stored value is a uuid.dropUtils.js resolveDropUuid · ItemDropZone.svelte handleDrop

Canonical spec
  • panel bg-0 · 1px border-strong · radius 11 · padding --fab-space-chip · shadow-lg
  • anchor portalled to the application root, measured against the scrolling panel, flipped and clamped — never a CSS offset
  • width trigger width, min 240 / max 340
  • grid an ICON SEARCH: square tiles that carry only the glyph or image, no text, each naming itself in a tooltip and in its accessible name, under the same header (query field and count) and footer (key hints and action) as the list form. The primitive owns the grid, its columns, the cursor and the keys; the tile's size follows from the panel width and columns
  • focus enters the search input on open, returns to the trigger on close — or, where the search field is suppressed, the TRIGGER is the combobox and holds it
  • cursor an inset accent outline on the active row, matching the grid form's own active tile — a different CHANNEL from the fill rungs, so it composes over a marked row rather than replacing its face
  • keys the holder consumes ↑↓, Home/End and ↵, plus ←→ in the grid form, and leaves every other key to the field — but those four are the CARET'S first: it takes each only from the edge at which the caret would not move, and never over a selection, and never with a modifier held, arrows included; ↵ alone is answered first, because on a trigger holder a declined ↵ activates the button and shuts the panel. A trigger holder has no caret and keeps the whole map at every caret position, and a CLOSED one answers the select-only combobox's opening keys: ↑↓, Home and End open the panel with the cursor on the row they name, Alt+↓ opens it with none
  • selection aria-activedescendant over role="listbox"; options are tabindex="-1" and NEVER take DOM focus — each declares data-keyboard-focus="true", because a tabindex="-1" non-form element is exactly the case Foundry does not recognise
  • The grid form’s count and key hints are drawn in --fab-text-muted; the shipped --fab-text-subtle measures 3.64–4.10:1 on bg-0, debt owned by issue 2368.

  • open bindable · onClose
  • source (query) — sync or async
  • as list | grid · value · multiple · stayOpen — value is the id, or the ARRAY of ids under multiple; stayOpen is the gate alone, for a caller whose chosen option leaves the option set
  • optionGroups · header and footer snippets
  • loading · error · emptyText — an async source has all three
  • Trigger sets aria-expanded, and takes aria-haspopup as a declared capability — dialog (default) or listbox. The value states what OPENS: a panel with a query field is a dialog, a bare option list is a listbox, so the two are not interchangeable and a caller passing listbox must also pass showSearch={false}
Why the focus model is mandatory, not a preference. Foundry treats an element as focused only if it is a form control, contentEditable, or a button with a form. Roving focus onto an option button re-arms the canvas bindings, so ↑↓ would pan the map. Keeping focus in the input is the only model that works — which is what the shipped popover already does, by design.components/SearchablePopover.svelte aria-activedescendant (24 importing files) · listboxNavigation.js · anchoredPopover.js · overlayBounds.js · iconPickerPopover.js · portal.js
Shipped, and what is still target. The activedescendant model and the key map SHIPPED: the holder — the search field, or the trigger where there is none, at six call sites — carries role="combobox", aria-controls and aria-activedescendant, and drops both while the empty branch renders in the list's place. The cursor is an inset accent outline, the same two declarations the grid form's own active tile draws above, because a listbox that also marks a current value has spent all three fill rungs. as="grid", horizontalAlign, the trigger and option snippets, filterOptions, the class props and the measured list flooring all shipped with it, which is what let the icon and source pickers collapse into this panel rather than remain look-alikes. multiple AND stayOpen SHIPPED at issue 1513, and the sentence this replaces went false in the same commit: it said multi-select stayed target because “the only multi-select in the corpus is an adjudicated non-member”, and that non-member is the caller the mode was built for. multiple drives aria-selected from MEMBERSHIP of value rather than from equality with it, emits aria-multiselectable on the listbox and keeps the panel open across choices; stayOpen is that last part alone, because a panel whose chosen option LEAVES the option set has no selection to announce. Both are additive and default-off, so the other 23 importers render exactly as they did. The player app’s component-sources picker is the first caller and commits on choose. The Journal’s run-type filter is the first FILTER on the mode (issue 1644): search suppressed, so it announces a listbox; each row drawn through the option snippet as a decorative <Checkbox>, the kind’s glyph, its name and a bare mono count; and a footer clear action, “Show all run types”. A columns outside two to six draws and maps one column. keyHints adds the footer row, its hints in --fab-text-muted for the cursor’s real key map, and footerAction is its one accent action, handed the panel’s close. anchor opens the panel from a control the caller owns, and the primitive then renders no trigger. The grid form is an icon search, and its one caller does not draw one. EssenceSourceSelector passes as="grid" with two columns and fills each cell with a 34px image beside the component’s name, at 14px, in a 44px tile, under a bare search field with no count and no footer. That is a two-column LIST of components with thumbnails laid out as a grid — a picker for choosing a named thing, which the list form already draws — not the square, text-free tile grid the specimen above specifies for finding an icon or an image by looking at it. Either that caller misuses the element, or it designed one incorrectly: if a component is chosen by name, it belongs in the list form with a portrait on its row, and the grid form is not the shape for it; if a component is chosen by how it looks, its tile should carry the image alone, with the name as a tooltip, and the panel should share the list form’s header and footer. TintPicker API
  • SHIPPED — read from the $props() of TintPicker.svelte as issue 2459 recomposed it, at six importing files: two open it as a popover, the biome edit palette by an anchor and the New-biome swatch through TintPickerButton.svelte’s trigger snippet, and four essence surfaces render it inline. TintPicker.svelte is this specimen; TintPickerButton.svelte is its single-caller trigger.
  • colorToken string, default 'sage' — the chosen preset, folded onto a member of the shared palette before it is compared, so an unknown key marks the fallback rather than nothing.
  • customColor string, default '' — the free hex beside the presets. Only a six-digit #RRGGBB value is honoured, upper-cased, because an unvalidated string cannot be guaranteed legible across all seven themes.
  • allowCustom boolean, default false — whether that field is offered at all. Only a caller whose stored model has a custom sibling passes true (the two gathering-biome pickers); every other caller, including the four inline essence surfaces, passes false or relies on the default, and the ten presets are the whole vocabulary.
  • unset boolean, default false — true when the caller holds no authored colour. Without it the fold above marks a preset for a model that has chosen nothing.
  • allowNone boolean, default false · noneSelected boolean or null, default null — the strip’s leading no-colour cell and whether it is marked. null derives the mark from unset, which is what every popover caller wants; an explicit false marks nothing at all, which is the only way to say “leave unchanged” on a bulk-edit stage where that and “clear the colour” are both “no preset is marked”.
  • layout popover | inline, default popover — inline renders the strip instead of the panel.
  • trigger snippet · anchor element or resolver · open bindable boolean, default false · bounds selector or resolver — forwarded to <SearchPopover> as they are, so a missing anchor is trigger mode. An anchor caller binds open and keeps its own control’s gesture; a trigger snippet spreads the primitive’s attributes on the caller’s own named button.
  • Event contract: onChange, default a no-op, receives the whole {colorToken, customColor} pair from a preset click and from a hex edit alike · onClear function or null, default null, is the unset instruction, deliberately NOT folded into onChange as an empty token because that would make every existing consumer learn a new falsy case. A pick closes the popover and returns focus to the control that opened it, and No colour calls onClear and then closes. The popover is the picker’s own panel, which measures, portals and dismisses itself, so there is no position or portal prop.
  • Accessible naming: every cell is a real <button> whose localized label is written as BOTH aria-label and title, since a swatch has no text of its own, and is named by presetGridLabel with its siblings: inline, each cell carries aria-pressed, true on the selected cell alone, in a group; in the popover, each tile is an option carrying aria-selected, true on the selected tile alone, in a listbox inside a dialog of the same name. No colour, the strip’s leading cell or the panel’s footer action, renders only when the gate is open AND a handler was supplied, because a control that does nothing is worse than none. customHexLabel names the hex field and noneLabel No colour. The three labels default to their localized English through localizeOr, so a caller passing none still names the palette.
  • Geometry: the popover is the picker panel at its 240px floor, its swatches radius 6 inside ~52px radius-9 square tiles, 3px inset (1px border + 2px padding); inline, each swatch is a 28px strip cell of at least 44px. The selected mark is a 2px inset ring drawn as an inset box-shadow on the swatch, in --fab-biome-icon-foreground on a colour and --fab-text on the no-colour cell; pointer hover keeps the outset accent outline, the keyboard cursor takes the picker’s inset outline (issue 2416), and no tick is drawn (issue 2257).
Menu API
  • SHIPPED — read from the $props() of ActionMenu.svelte, which claims this entry at issue 1516; the drawing above is its shipped panel (issue 2257).
  • Props: items an ordered list of {id, label, icon?, disabled?, danger?, tone?, data?}, each label already localized, a tone — one of the five kind tones component, tag, essence, currency and knowledge, or none at rest — tinting that item’s glyph and never its label · ariaLabel, the default trigger’s required name · panelLabel, the menu’s name, or heading, an eyebrow in the panel and outside the menu that names it instead · trigger, a snippet for the caller’s own labelled trigger, handed the popup and expanded state, the handlers and the element binding · align, end (the default, for a kebab at a row’s end) or start (for an adder at a list’s start), the trigger edge the panel lines up with, clamped inside the host · triggerClass, triggerIcon, triggerTitle and triggerProps for the default icon trigger · menuClass on the portaled panel · open, bindable · disabled. It measures and portals itself against its own trigger, so it takes no anchor, and it marks no current value: the focused item takes the raised fill.
  • Event contract: onSelect receives the item’s id and is not called for a disabled item. An outside click closes the menu, and Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger.
  • Accessible naming: the panel is a menu named by its label or its heading, and each row is a menu item; a disabled row states it rather than being removed, so the set a reader walks is the set a reader was offered. The opening control carries the popup and expanded state, which the primitive hands a caller’s own trigger.
The swatch cursor is the picker cursor now, the swatch highlight used to animate, and the panel is the picker’s grid form. A swatch marks its keyboard cursor with the 2px accent outline INSET by 2px that <SearchPopover> puts on its active row, converged at issue 2416, and marks pointer hover with an OUTSET 2px accent outline at a 1px offset; a focused swatch under the pointer keeps the cursor. Hover is the outline alone and never fills: the maintainer ruled on 2026-10-11 that a swatch’s colour must never change on hover, so the picker’s --fab-surface-raised row fill does not carry over, and the shipped swatch, which declares no hover background, already holds it. The animation is not authored here: Foundry core sets transition: 0.5s on every button and .manager-color-preset never resets it, so the outline’s width and offset tweened in over half a second whenever the pointer or focus arrived. The animation is fixed: .manager-color-preset and the .manager-color-picker-trigger that opens the popover now declare transition: none, in the popover and the inline strip alike, because both draw these cells. The panel shipped at issue 2459: the live popover is the grid form of <SearchPopover>, on the picker’s own panel, header, tiles and footer, as the target specimen draws it, and the hand-built --fab-bg-3 box is gone. The offering rule settled at issue 2352: the palette offers ten tints, and only the gathering biome, whose stored option carries a customColor sibling, offers a free hex. Shipped, with listed differences: the live count is drawn in --fab-text-subtle where the target specimen draws --fab-text-muted, debt owned by issue 2368, and the live panel places the count above the query field and draws a 30px field at radius 7, where the target specimen draws the count beside a 34px field at radius 9.fabricate.css .manager-color-preset:focus-visible (the inset cursor) · fabricate.css .manager-color-preset:hover (the outset outline) · fabricate.css .manager-travel-option[data-active-option='true'] (the picker’s cursor) · TintPicker.svelte
One control the set needs. <Menu> is what <PickerRow>’s allowAny opens — eight callers across three studios. <TintPicker> ships allowCustom false by default; the two gathering-biome pickers opt in, and the four inline essence surfaces pass false explicitly.TintPicker.svelte, the specimen · TintPickerButton.svelte, its single-caller trigger · managerColorTokens.js MANAGER_COLOR_TOKENS

Marks & atoms

Eight marks, routed by job rather than by eye. The domain model defines the Rail Marker Family; that vocabulary is canon and the rest resolve against it.

Incomplete and Blocked are the states a plain toggle could never express, and they are why this is not a styled switch. Locked states its reason in place, not in a tooltip.
Two rules that keep the marks apart. A list row gets a status button and the record’s own editor gets a toggle.
