<Chip>

Chip · shipped

The app’s ONE chip, and the highest-traffic primitive in the set at 111 importing files. It carries a count, a state, a category or a tag, on one geometry: issue 883 extracted it because the chip had drifted into two scales, and issue 1506 retired four status pills into it — the manager’s, the journal’s run pill, the crafting status badge and the crafting quantity tag — so a record’s STATE and a record’s TAG are now the same component. Three axes, and none of them may move another: tone is colour, emphasis is how that colour arrives, density is the scale. A tone that resized, or a density that repainted, is the drift this entry exists to end.

tones — thirteen families, colour and nothing else
Enabled Incomplete Blocked DC 15 Applies to Extract
Thirteen names plus the default: active positive disabled warning info danger neutral negative accent muted tag secondary subtle. An unrecognised value renders the default chip rather than an unpainted class, so a typo reads as a miss instead of doing nothing.
the recessive ladder — four ranks, routed by meaning
Salvage mode 2 steps Not in system Salvage · n/a
secondary → neutral → subtle → muted, loudest to quietest. It is an ORDER and never a set of percentages: five theme roots state it as one opaque hue at three descending percentages of itself, one mixes two percentages over a different base triple, and one states the first three as three DIFFERENT opaque hues plus one alpha — where an alpha comparison ties three of the four. The quantity that orders them is each ink’s CONTRAST composited over that theme’s own ground.
densities — seven scales, one chip
default row list action header tag-run inspector
In ladder values: default 20 high / r10 / 9.92px-700 / 4px 6px; row 22 / r999 / 10px-600 / 0 9px; list 18.4 bordered / 16.4 bare / r999 / 9px-600 / line-height 1.6 / 1px 8px, single-line; action 34 / r9 / 0.72rem / 0 var(--fab-space-3) — the button’s geometry in full, because it stands in a row with Back, Delete and Save, and truncate keeps the button’s corner at this density; header the same at 38, the page header’s rung beside its 38px actions, while an edit card’s cluster keeps action (issue 2257 D10); tag-run ~25 / r999 / 11px-600 / 6px 12px / a 9px leading glyph, the prototype’s value where this entry was silent (maintainer ruling 2026-09-28); inspector 20 / r999 / 10px-600 / 4px 8px. The default’s 10px corner and 999px are the SAME rendered corner at a single line, and diverge only once a chip wraps. Issue 1648 makes the list specimen's inherited 1.6 explicit in both specimen and component, correcting the contradictory ~13 prose. Issue 2257 adds header (D10).
emphasis — four alternatives, not a composition
outlined lit bare Have3 Need2
outlined states ONLY the fill — a flat --fab-bg-1 plate — so the tone keeps its edge and its ink, for a badge standing on a panel of its own family. lit puts the chip’s own colour on the ink over a 16% wash of it, and reaches only the two chips that declare a colour: tone="tag" and any swatch or tint. bare is border: 0 and nothing else, for the edgeless badge a dense list row draws; its glyph takes 7px. Bare is the ONE emphasis that does not compose with struck, because its border shorthand resets the dashed border-style that prop states. solid is an opaque ground, for a chip read over artwork of unknown colour: a coloured tone is filled with its own colour — --fab-success, --fab-info, --fab-danger, --fab-accent, --fab-warning — and inked with that theme’s --fab-on-* ink, which is the page ground in this palette and is what the warning fill takes in every theme because no on-warning ink is declared; a toneless or recessive chip stands on --fab-bg-3, keeps its own edge and is inked --fab-text whichever recessive tone it carries, because every weaker rung of that ladder falls below 4.5:1 on the raised ground at this size in at least one shipped theme. It states no geometry, so the pair drawn here is density="list" with solid.
icon only — a square, one side per density
SEVEN icon-only sides are published: 20 default, 22 row, 15 list, 34 action, 38 header, 25 tag-run, 20 inspector. The list square is independently specified at 15px and remains so when the labelled list specimen's 1.6 line-height is made explicit; it is not the labelled chip's 18.4px bordered height.
removable — a membership token in an editable set
Perception Survival Athletics
A chip in an EDITABLE SET — a value a GM authored here and can take back — and the only chip that carries a remove control. The read-only state chip above never takes one: spec.md routes a record’s state to this chip’s TONE, and a fact the GM cannot delete gets no delete affordance, so a fact chip that grew an x would offer an edit the screen cannot honour. The hit box is a 20px square at the compact density and at every other one, because the density axis scales the badge you READ and never the control you PRESS; the chip’s own box follows it to 28px, which is the shipped availability pill’s height to the pixel, and the 20px side is the default density’s own min-height and the iconOnly square already published above. And truncate clips the LABEL, never the control: the label takes a clipping box of its own and the remove control is flex: 0 0 auto, so a long authored name is cut at the label’s edge and the x keeps its full square at every width.
Canonical spec
  • one chip every badge, count, state, category and tag in both windows is this component; a second pill component is a missing DENSITY here, never a new entry
  • three axes tone colour, emphasis how it arrives, density scale — each closed, each independent, none of them geometry-and-paint at once
  • routed by meaning the four recessive tones are an ordered ladder and a caller picks by what it MEANS, never by matching a tone name to a token name: muted inks with --fab-text-disabled and neutral with --fab-text-muted, so only subtle and secondary are spelled like the token they use
  • accent inks with --fab-accent-text, not the family base, because the raw accent over --fab-accent-soft measures under AA at this type size
  • position is the caller’s, geometry is not a call site may set flex, a width or a margin from outside; it may never restate a size, a corner or a face
  • row composes with a tone the row density states its ground and ink ahead of the tones, so a tone paints a row chip as it paints every other density — the positive, struck and warning chips of <RouteSources> are row chips
  • icon only requires a name the glyph is aria-hidden, so an icon-only chip states aria-label at every tag; a title is a tooltip and not a name
  • removable is a MEMBERSHIP TOKEN the chip is one member of an editable set and its x takes that member out; the read-only state chip is this same component saying something the GM cannot delete, and it never takes removable
  • refused on an operable host tag="button" or tag="a" would nest a button inside a control, so the component THROWS rather than dropping the prop — and the same throw refuses a removable chip whose control has no accessible name, or no handler to act on, because a remove control that cannot be announced or cannot act is a defect rather than a degraded mode. It enforces at the primitive where iconOnly above states its half and leaves it to a source contract, and the difference is that this prop has no shipped callers to be retroactive to
  • the live region is the CALLER’s neither adding nor removing a member moves focus into the row, so an editable set owes ONE aria-live="polite" summary beside it; a bare chip cannot own one, and a region wrapped around the row announces each added chip’s whole subtree — its remove control’s label included — and nothing at all on a removal
  • focus survives the removal the next chip’s remove control, else the previous chip’s, else the nearest enclosing data-chip-remove-fallback, moved BEFORE the handler runs. Deleting the focused button drops focus to <body>, where Foundry treats the window as unfocused and the next keystroke reaches the canvas bindings. The ROW itself is not a rung the chip can add: it cannot put a tabindex on markup it does not own, which is why the third rung is a hook the caller puts on its own add trigger
Svelte API
  • SHIPPED — read from components/Chip.svelte’s $props() at issue 1506.
  • tag the rendered element — span (default), or li / button / div where the surrounding markup demands it: a chip inside a role="list" is a list item and a clickable chip is a real button
  • tone the colour family without its is- prefix — the thirteen above, or '' for the default fill. Colour ONLY; a tone never changes a size
  • emphasis '' | outlined | lit | bare | solid — four values, alternatives rather than a composition. An unrecognised value resolves to '', exactly as an unrecognised tone does
  • density default | row | list | action | header | tag-run | inspector — seven; a further scale is a new entry rather than a new value (the seventh, header, by issue 2257 D10)
  • presentation '' (default) or clock: opt-in read-only WorldClockChip composition, 28px border-box/min-height, radius 7, space-2 gap/horizontal padding, centring one baseline-aligned line of icon, label and value. It owns geometry at Chip rather than relying on a losing caller override; ordinary density callers retain their defaults.
  • iconOnly the chip IS its glyph: equal insets, no label, the square side of whichever density it is drawn at. A BOOLEAN and not a density, because it is not a scale. It REQUIRES aria-label, and emits role="img" only where the chip is non-interactive — on tag="button" or "a" the label is already the control’s name and an img role would announce an operable control as a picture. The role is written BEFORE the rest spread, so a role a caller passes is never overridden
  • icon Font Awesome classes for a leading glyph. A fa-circle passed here is a MARK rather than a glyph and draws at 0.36rem through a rule of the primitive’s own; a fa-circle a caller slots into the children is the caller’s and is untouched
  • swatch · tint a bare --fab-tag-* palette key. swatch draws a leading colour DOT — this chip is ABOUT a colour; tint inks the whole chip — this chip IS that colour. Both ride one validated --fab-chip-color declaration, and anything that is not a bare key is DROPPED rather than emitted
  • mono numerals in the mono face with tabular-nums, so columns of counts and DCs line up · truncate opt-in single line that keeps its glyph and the start of its label and ends in an ellipsis, which also returns the stadium · struck the dashed-edge, struck-through MUTED variant for a value switched off in the scope being read
  • class additional classes for a caller that needs layout context from the global sheet · element bindable, the rendered DOM node, because bind:this on a component yields the instance and a caller that must measure or focus the chip has no other route
  • removable · removeLabel · onRemove the editable-set form. removable adds is-removable and a trailing button.manager-chip-remove carrying data-chip-remove and data-keyboard-focus="true" — a button OUTSIDE a form, which Foundry’s hasFocus recognises only by its form, so without the declaration Space pauses the game and the arrows pan the canvas while the control holds focus. removeLabel is that control’s aria-label and names the member it takes out (“Remove Perception”), because the chip’s label arrives as a snippet and no component can read a name out of one; onRemove is called once focus has moved. It defaults to undefined and the attribute is written {removeLabel || undefined}: an aria-label="" REPLACES the name an element would take from its own content rather than falling back to it, and a generic default — even a localized one — names eight chips in a row identically. This is the “the caller always has a better name than the primitive could invent” case, so the name is required rather than invented, and the refusal is what makes that real. The three are REQUIRED together, and the refusals above are one throw
  • disabled a declared prop rather than a rest-spread attribute as of issue 1515, because the remove control has to go inert WITH the chip. It still lands on the rendered element exactly where the spread used to put it, written before the spread beside role
  • every other attribute — title, aria-*, data-* hooks, onclick, type — lands on the rendered element through the rest spread
The manager chip carries a colour as tint — a bare --fab-tag-* key that inks glyph and label over the quiet surface behind the plain hairline (issue 1371, maintainer ruling M29). An essence drawn that way is the <EssenceChip> entry below, which owns the essence-to-chip mapping and adds no geometry of its own. And the class hook is manager-chip in both windows, which is a measurement rather than an oversight: the smoke harness, the mounted suites and the layout ratchet all pin that literal, and two shipped components/ controls render this chip into the player window, so renaming the hook would break the pins without changing anything a user sees. The solid emphasis arrived at issue 1518, as the opaque ground a held-versus-needed count is read on over artwork; it was added opt-in, so no chip that shipped before it changed its paint. Issue 1518 then moved the have/need chips in IoTable, IngredientOptionSelector and ShoppingList, and the recipe header’s status pip, onto it.91 importers · Chip.svelte · retired into it at issue 1506, by render site: the manager status pill (36), the journal run pill (4), the crafting status badge (2), the crafting quantity tag (6)

Kicker API
  • SHIPPED — read from components/Kicker.svelte’s $props() at issue 1505.
  • as p | span | h3 — the ELEMENT it renders, because a micro-label is sometimes a heading and sometimes not. The union is MEASURED rather than forward-looking: across the corpus the hosts are 62 p, 3 span and 1 h3, so h2 and h4 have no caller and are withdrawn. h3 is the one member of that measured union NO shipped caller reaches — of the seventeen shipped sites nine pass p and eight pass span — and it is kept on the measurement rather than on a call site. An unrecognised value renders p.
  • tone default | accent — the INK and nothing else. A tone that changed the size would reintroduce the drift this component removes.
  • children the label text, already localized by the caller. A nested child is legitimate and is how the recipe-item editor keeps its “· from linked item” note, which declares no size and therefore inherits this one’s 8.5px.
  • a rest spread on the root — it carries the data-* hook a harness or a capture step selects on, so the attribute is genuinely ABSENT when unset. A call site writes the hook with an EMPTY STRING, data-x="", so a hook written bare on the element this replaces still renders data-x="" rather than the data-x="true" a bare attribute on a component tag produces.
  • TARGET — none. There is no class and no style: a caller that needs LAYOUT — a flex row, an ellipsis, a min-width — keeps its OWN wrapper element and nests this inside it, which is the shape the kicker specimen above already draws. It declares margin: 0, which this page’s geometry does not, because the specimen draws the kicker only as a span while nine of the seventeen converted sites are a p that zeroes the user-agent margin itself today. Recorded deviation: it also declares line-height: 1.3, which this page’s .k-kicker rule omits because this page never draws a WRAPPED kicker. Every stat box label wraps to two lines in the player Shopping list, and without it each one inherits its host’s ~1.5 — about 12.75px of leading on 8.5px type, which reads as two loose lines rather than one label. The rules this component replaces declared 1.2.
IconChip API
  • SHIPPED — read from components/Medallion.svelte’s $props() at issue 1506, which retired the two crafting thumbnails into it and made it the app’s ONE art tile at 63 render sites.
  • art the resolved image path; falsy takes the GLYPH fallback. Named art rather than src because what it carries is a record’s ARTWORK and not an element’s attribute. src is a DEPRECATED alias kept for one release; art wins where both are passed and no shipped call site uses it.
  • alt the image’s alt text, passed EXPLICITLY wherever art is set. alt="" is the correct value at every shipped site — each renders the record’s name as adjacent text — and the contract is that the decision was TAKEN, not that a sentence was written. A source contract reds on an art-bearing call site that names no alt, and on one reaching for the deprecated alias to escape it.
  • icon the Font Awesome class drawn when there is no art · size the edge length in px, default 40 — which is OFF the published ladder above, and which no call site takes: every call site passes its own ladder size · glyph the glyph’s font-size in px for a tile large enough that the 0.9rem default reads as a speck. Both numbers are coerced and floored at zero before they reach the style attribute.
  • tint a bare --fab-tag-* palette key, or '' for the accent default. It recolours the GLYPH and nothing else (issue 1506): every tinted example on this page renders the tile on the flat surface and sets color: alone, and the reference’s row chips share ONE surface and differ in the glyph. Unset is byte-identical to what shipped, because the glyph reads the token through a var() fallback. The default accent glyph computes to 2.85:1 on bg-3 in the ironblood-forge palette and 2.51:1 in the hearth-herb palette, where text-secondary would give 4.06:1 and 3.51:1, read from fabricate-tokens.css; the glyph is decorative, so the 3:1 non-text floor does not bind it.
  • variant '' (the artwork tile) or glyph-chip — the tile as an UNBORDERED slate chip carrying a tinted glyph. The absent border is the whole of it: the size and the colour are the props above, and making either implicit here would put a second copy of a row’s geometry inside a primitive that already takes it as an argument.
  • tone '', success, danger or accent — paints the edge, the ground and the glyph in that family’s -border, -soft and -text tokens, as the toned specimens on this page do by hand, and it outranks tint. A glyph-chip variant draws no edge, so a tone shows its ground and glyph alone. The Checks Studio’s rolled count dice read qualified or cancelled by it (issue 2004), and a chosen <OptionCards> chip is accent (issue 2467); anything else resolves to '', which is byte-identical to what shipped.
  • ink '', success, danger or neutral — inks the GLYPH alone in that family’s -text token, the ink a small mark takes, or in --fab-text-secondary for neutral, and leaves the edge and the slate ground as they are; it outranks tint. A resting <OptionCards> chip is neutral (issue 2467). The Checks Studio’s rolled result card draws its success or failure icon with it on the shared 30px tile, with no variant (issue 2080); where tone already paints the glyph, the ink wins. Anything else resolves to '', which is byte-identical to what shipped.
  • TARGET — none, and there is deliberately no class, no style and no rest spread. It is an IMPORT-FREE LEAF: the CALLER resolves the image and passes a plain string, because importing the shared art resolver here would propagate a required raw-module entry into every mount harness that compiles anything rendering this tile.
StatBox API
  • SHIPPED — read from components/StatBox.svelte’s $props() at issue 1505.
  • value · label — the figure and the micro-label beneath it. The label IS a <Kicker>, composed rather than restated, which is what the specimen above draws.
  • icon a leading glyph on the value line. A recorded deviation from the geometry above, which draws none: the Shopping list renders one in all three cards, and without the prop the conversion silently drops three glyphs.
  • tone default | info | danger — also a recorded deviation, since .k-stat declares no tone variant at all. Each value is derived from a shipped caller state: info is the item page’s accented figure, danger the Shopping list’s alert card. Every tone paints the value’s ink; danger additionally paints the edge, the fill and the glyph, because that caller tints the whole card. An unrecognised value renders default.
  • a rest spread on the box root, carrying its data-* hook written data-x="" · valueDataAttr on the value · labelDataAttr, forwarded into the composed <Kicker> — the hooks that let a conversion preserve every existing data-* attribute verbatim, on the elements this component itself renders. Attribute-only: they carry no behaviour, and every literal value a call site passes to either DataAttr prop must start with data-.
  • Recorded deviation: the value carries font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums, which the geometry above omits but both callers declare — “so a 9 → 10 change cannot reflow the tile”. Three numerals in a three-column grid is where tabular figures matter most.
  • TARGET — none, and four names are WITHDRAWN rather than carried: size, unit, tone="warning" and tone="accent". No caller in the corpus reaches any of them and no test acts on one, and a prop nothing reaches is the unreachable configuration this reference exists to prevent. It emits no interactive element and takes no handler, which is the rule above stated as a contract rather than as a caption.
Both marks reached the player window at issue 1514, and the art tile reached it hardest. Counts measured by componentImporters.js at the tip: IconChip 53 importing files over 77 render sites, 32 of those files and 49 of those sites in the player window; Kicker 24 files over 37 sites, 22 files and 33 sites there; StatBox unmoved at 2 files, one of them the crafting shopping summary. Three facts came out of the eyebrow conversions that this block did not state. The test is a LINE BOX, not a font size — seventeen of the candidates are block hosts whose line box IS a row in a column stack, so the published bands are 12px→11.05, 11px→11.05, 10px→11.05 and a line-height: 1 band that GROWS from 10 to 11.05; an as="span" site is measured against its host block’s strut instead, which is why StatBox re-declares the same 1.3 on the label it composes. The rule being replaced is swept for margin and for type it sets on SIBLINGS, and both bit: two candidates in the alchemy workbench carried a margin this component hard-declares away, and one inventory row set text-transform and letter-spacing on the ROW, so moving the type onto this component silently un-capitalised the sibling beside it and cut its box 89.52px to 55.64px. And the host set is a REFUSAL, not a fallback to live with: three <h4> candidates and one <label for> bound to a select were declined rather than converted, because {p, span, h3} silently falls back to p and would have dropped a heading out of the outline or a select’s accessible name with it. And the ink is the SECOND correction to the geometry above, on a contrast reading. The conversions were first taken with the specimen’s --fab-text-subtle, moving 41 player-facing labels from --fab-text-muted at 12px to the subtle tone at 8.5px and 10px. Six of the seven palettes declare muted and subtle as ALPHAS over the surface — which is the token census stated earlier in this section, read for this question — so on the default fabricate theme that composites to 3.69:1 on --fab-surface and 3.50:1 on --fab-surface-soft — under the 4.5:1 small-text floor spec.md states, at the smallest type the product draws. The muted tone reads 5.42:1 and 5.00:1 at the same two grounds and clears the floor in all seven palettes, the worst being ironblood-forge at 5.19:1 and 4.77:1. ONE palette is what hid it, and naming it is what makes the reading checkable: mythwright alone states those two tones as opaque hues, and it is the only palette of the seven whose subtle tone clears the floor at all, reading 5.28:1 from the same declaration. Six fail and one passes, so the specimen was set from the single outlier. Corrected here and on the component, so it also moves the two sites the conversion never touched — the manager’s recipe-item Overview tab and the label StatBox composes. Empty’s note and filtered variants carry the same correction on the same measurement, against proto:2262 and proto:2545.Measured in the View Lab per site; the crafting shopping titles moved 13.75 to 11.05 with the tracking 0.55px to 0.935px

EssenceChip · shipped

An essence drawn as a chip, in the colour the world Essence Catalogue gave it, carrying its glyph and — where the caller has one — its quantity. The maintainer’s third live test found the rules library’s row chips, the rules editor’s tiles and the inspector’s essence line all grey while the world bulk panel alone drew the colour (issue 1371, maintainer ruling M29); every site had written its own essence-to-chip mapping and every one had forgotten the colour. This is that mapping written once, over the manager chip’s tint axis, and it carries no chip geometry of its own.

  • colour the essence’s colorToken, a bare --fab-tag-* key, as the chip’s tint; unauthored is untinted

Why a composition and not a second chip. The hand-rolled-chip ratchet is what keeps the manager at one pill, and a second component that declared chip geometry would be the drift it exists to catch. What no primitive owned was the ESSENCE half — which glyph, which colour, which words a screen reader hears — and three sites had each answered it differently. Its one style is the count’s mono face, declared on the count alone so a chip that also shows the name keeps the name in the chip’s own face. One site is deferred, and this is where that is said. apps/alchemy/EssenceChips.svelte is by its own docblock “a compact, presentational row of essence icon+count chips” with a colorToken tint (issue 917) and FOUR call sites in the player app, and it is not converted here: it belongs to the player app’s visual language rather than the manager’s, it tints through its own --alchemy-essence-color vehicle rather than this chip’s tint, and converting it is a player-app decision with its own frames rather than a side effect of M29. Meter · shippedBandedBar · shippedStageBars · shipped

Four instruments, three components. Merging them leaves one component unable to carry one correct accessible role, which is why the shipped fill leaf renders none.

Meter API
  • SHIPPED — read from Meter.svelte’s $props() at issue 2182, which drew its segments. The shared fill leaf FillBar.svelte renders no role deliberately, so this component owns the one it needs.
  • Props: value and max, the fill being their ratio and a max of zero reading full · segments an ordered list of entries drawn as the one fill’s segments, left to right, each entry a semantic tone or a caller-owned color and a value on the scale of max: each entry but the last spans its value, stopping where the fill ends, and the last spans the rest of the reading, so the segments always make up the fill; an entry that spans nothing is not drawn, when none spans anything the fill takes the first entry’s paint, and the segments abut with no gap · valueText the caller-formatted reading (7 / 11) — caller-formatted because a ratio and a duration are two sentences and neither is arithmetic this component should do · exactly one of labelId, the id of the head the caller already renders above the track, or label, rendered visually hidden.
  • Passthrough: class plus a rest spread on the root, written after the class — the spread carries the data-* hook a harness or a capture step selects on, so the attribute is genuinely absent when unset.
  • Event contract: none. A meter is stated, never operated, so it takes no callback and emits no control; a figure a user can change belongs to a stepper or a band strip.
  • Accessible naming: the root carries the meter role with its own aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and an aria-valuetext equal to the reading, and it is named by the label the caller renders rather than by a duplicate string. The value and its label are always present as text, so colour is never the only encoding. A meter in segments still announces one reading: the segments are colour and width, so the caller states each one in valueText and as text beside the track. Neighbouring segments are not held to a contrast step against each other, so that text is the reading, not a legend.
BandedBar API
  • SHIPPED — read from BandedBar.svelte’s $props() at issue 1782; the two banded units above are the same component with the ramp read in two directions.
  • Props: rows an ordered list, each a band name, a percent and the fill its whole track takes — a semantic tone or a ramp key resolved by util/dropRateTier.js, never interpolated, so 57% and 58% cannot land in a colour the ramp does not contain · direction ascending (a drop rate: better is rarer) or descending (a risk: the hazard at a high chance, so a glance down a tool list sorts itself), which reads a row’s fill off the ramp when the row names none · density, forwarded to the fill leaf.
  • Passthrough: class plus a rest spread on the root, written after the class — the spread carries the data-* hook a harness or a capture step selects on, so the attribute is genuinely absent when unset.
  • Event contract: none, for the reason the meter states.
  • Accessible naming: a single chance bar is a meter carrying its own aria-valuenow, named by its caption or by a rest aria-label; a histogram of bands is decorative and its tracks are hidden from assistive technology, because each row already states its band name and its percentage as adjacent text and announcing the fill again says nothing new. Which of the two a caller gets follows from rows holding one entry or several rather than from a prop; at compact density the one row keeps the meter role but draws the histogram’s band row, so a one-outcome odds chart reads like its neighbours. Every row, a single one included, carries data-banded-bar-row, -track and -percent keyed by its id or its index, so a hook survives a chart collapsing to one row.
StageBars API
  • SHIPPED — read from StageBars.svelte’s $props() at issue 1782. It is one bar per stage side by side, not one track with dividers: the earlier single-track version hid a divider inside a bar until the fill reached it.
  • Props: stages an ordered list, each an optional localized name, the visible caption, an optional label, the bar’s accessible name, an optional localized valueText, the bar’s reading in place of its percentage, and a value from 0 to 100, where an unfilled stage still renders its own bar and still reads as a stage · currentIndex the stage being worked · numbered whether the caption beneath each bar carries its position and name, which the specimen draws, a named caption carrying its stage’s name as its title · exactly one of ariaLabel or ariaLabelledBy, the latter where the caller renders the kicker.
  • Passthrough: class plus a rest spread on the root, written after the class — the spread carries the data-* hook a harness or a capture step selects on, so the attribute is genuinely absent when unset.
  • Event contract: none. This is the progress instrument; choosing which stage is on screen belongs to <StageNav>, and merging the two would give one component two roles.
  • Accessible naming: the row is a group with a required localized label, and each bar is a progress indicator carrying its own value, named by its stage’s label, else its name; the one bar of a one-stage group with neither takes the group’s own name, and an unnamed stage of several has none, so its caller passes label: <RunProgress> passes “Stage n of m” through the FABRICATE.Common.StageBars.Unnamed key (issue 2455). A bar’s reading is its stage’s valueText, written as aria-valuetext, where it is a non-empty string, and its percentage otherwise, as <Meter>’s caller-formatted reading is. A named caption is ellipsized on overflow with its stage’s name as its title, as an entry’s time is; the caption stays aria-hidden, so the title is a pointer affordance (issue 2610). The current stage’s bar carries aria-current="step", so the stage being worked is not told by colour alone. The captions beneath are the sighted reading, so a run’s position is legible without the fills. Inside the run card, a role="button", the group and its bars are presentational and the card’s Step n of m text is the reading; the run detail is where they are exposed.
Why three, not one. The shipped fill leaf renders no role deliberately, “because the accessible semantics differ per site” — a chance bar is a meter with its own valuenow, an odds histogram row is decorative. Three components, three roles; the shared leaf stays presentational underneath them. Colour is never the only encoding — the value and its band name are always present as text.FillBar.svelte header
The shared fill leaf reaches three importers, all of them these instruments. Issue 1514 converted four hand-rolled tracks onto the leaf, and issue 1782 moved three of them onto the entries above: the journal run card’s and run detail’s stage tracks onto StageBars through RunProgress, and the crafting essence pool’s per-essence meter and the actor bar’s stamina track onto Meter, beside the journal’s own EssencePool; the gathering chance bar and the Checks Studio’s odds rows are BandedBar. The fourth importer, the gathering tab’s per-drop chance track, left at issue 1644: the find list states each chance as a figure on <YieldScale>. A caller owns the WIDTH. The leaf and each instrument are flex:1 1 auto, so the stamina track keeps its 72px wrapper as a width pin and the meter fills it. And a state painted in CSS is a prop. A caller’s scoped block cannot reach the leaf’s element, so a meter’s fill state arrives as a segment’s tone or color, and the event scale’s middle step is the named theme colour --fab-hazard-mid rather than a mix. One gap is recorded rather than worked around: two of the four hand-rolled fills declared a transition: width, one with a prefers-reduced-motion escape, and the leaf declares neither — so both bars move instantly. Moved: the run card and run detail stage tracks, whose gap is --fab-space-chip rather than --fab-space-1; every other instrument site renders unmoved.Measured in the View Lab at issue 1782

<WorldClockChip>

shipped

The hour the world is at. It appears wherever time decides an outcome — a run counting down, a gathering window, a downtime day — and it is stated, never operated, in a player window.

the chip
World clockDay 14 · 08:00
28 at radius 7, the info family throughout: an 11px glyph, a label naming what the number is and the number itself in mono, on one baseline. It is a mark rather than a control: no stepper, no arrows, no advance button anywhere in a player window.
Canonical spec
  • chip 28 · radius 7 · info fill, border and ink, centring one baseline-aligned line of glyph, label and value
  • glyph 11px in --fab-info-text, centred on the line: an optical correction, since a Font Awesome glyph’s ink is not centred in its em box
  • label 9px, 700, 0.08em, uppercase, in --fab-info-text: a deliberate info-toned kicker scale, kept apart from <Kicker> (8.5px, 0.11em, muted, no info tone).
  • value mono, tabular numerals — it is compared across visits
  • player window read-only, always; the GM owns advancing it
Svelte API
  • Read from WorldClockChip.svelte’s $props() at issue 1644.
  • value the formatted world time — a pre-localized string
  • label required — the kicker text
  • icon Font Awesome classes, default fas fa-clock
  • No events and no rest spread. A surface that needs to advance the clock is a GM surface and uses its own control.
Why the player window has no clock control. Time is shared world state. A player advancing it to finish their own run advances every other run at the table, which is a GM decision with no player-side undo. The chip therefore reports and the rail carries the bolt, so nothing about a self-completing run is a surprise without also being a player’s own earlier choice.
Measured at issue 1644; shipped at issue 2257. On ready-single the chip is 28 at radius 7 in the info fill, border and ink, with 8px padding and gap and a mono 10.5/500 tabular value, drawn through Chip’s presentation="clock". The specimen is redrawn to its 11px glyph and its 9px, 0.08em label, both in --fab-info-text (D22): the glyph’s size is the optical correction its header records, and the label is 9px, 700, 0.08em, uppercase, in --fab-info-text: a deliberate info-toned kicker scale, kept apart from <Kicker> (8.5px, 0.11em, muted, no info tone). Glyph, label and value measure 7.11–13.92:1 on the info chip over the clock topbar in all seven themes (world-clock-chip-contrast.test.js). The bolt ships on the Journal’s run card at issue 1644, drawn only for a run the world-time scan will take whose current stage carries no automatic blocker, so it reads “Finishes this stage as time passes”. It is drawn under <ListRow>’s selectable dense unit.

<DiceTiles>

shipped

The dice of a success-counting roll, one tile per die, each stating what it did. A count is only checkable when a reader can see which dice made it, so the tiles are the evidence, and they read the same in the Checks Studio simulator, the player’s result box and the chat card (issue 2006).

combined marks — each explosion’s die straight after its parent
8101011392
qualified · cancelled · exploded Six d10s at 8 or better, tens exploding and ones cancelling: 8 10 1 3 9 2, the 10 exploding into a 10 that explodes into a 1. A die carries every mark it earned on ONE tile, and a die an explosion rolled is its own tile immediately after the die that rolled it, so the order reads as the dice fell. The legend under the tiles is optional: the result box and the simulator draw it, chat does not.
bought dice — the border dashed, its tone kept
120114
qualified · cancelled · exploded · dashed = bought Four d20s at 14 or under, the last two bought with additional dice (issue 2008): 1 20 11 4. A bought die is one of the last original dice in roll order; it dashes the border its tone already gives it and draws no glyph, its label ends bought, and an explosion it rolls is a generated die, not a bought one. The legend gains dashed = bought only when the roll bought a die, and nothing is marked bought on a secret or non-public roll.
a 280px chat column — wrapping, and the cap
123456789101234+985 more
The tiles wrap inside their host and never scroll sideways. The model holds at most 40 tiles and states the rest as +{n} more; the Count row beside it always states the full totals, because a pool can reach 999 dice and card content is persisted.
Canonical spec
  • tile 38 wide at least, 44 high, radius 9; the face in mono at 14px and 500, the marks at 9px beneath it
  • tone a cancel reads danger; a qualifying or exploding die success, its face in the same success ink as the tile; any other die the plain hairline and muted ink
  • marks Font Awesome Free fa-check, fa-xmark and fa-rotate, every glyph aria-hidden
  • list the tiles are list items and each one’s aria-label names its face, every mark, and rolled by an explosion for a generated die, so colour is never the only signal
  • bought a die bought with additional dice keeps its tone and dashes its border, carries the bought token in its marks hook and ends its aria-label , bought; an explosion it rolls is generated, not bought
  • classes one fabricate-dice-tiles family and never Foundry’s own .dice-rolls .roll or .dice-total.success, so nothing of Foundry is inherited or restyled
Svelte API
  • SHIPPED — read from components/DiceTiles.svelte’s $props() at issue 2006 task 6.
  • model { tiles: [{ face, marks, generated, bought? }], more, bought? } — tileModel(countDisplay) from src/ui/presenters/countDiceTiles.js, which orders the executed projection’s active dice, marks its last countDisplay.bought original dice bought and caps them at 40. Nothing renders without a tile.
  • legend boolean, default off — the key under the tiles, each mark keyed by the very glyph its tile draws (aria-hidden) beside its word, ending dashed = bought when the model bought a die (issue 2134).
  • faceDataAttr · marksDataAttr · legendDataAttr — a host’s own hook names, defaulting to data-dice-tile-face, data-dice-tile-marks (space-separated) and data-dice-tiles-legend. A generated tile always carries data-dice-tile-generated, and the overflow item data-dice-tiles-more.
  • renderDiceTilesHtml(model, localize, { legend }) — the escaped chat renderer, writing the markup this component renders.
  • No events and no control: the tiles are a record.
Why a primitive and not an art tile. <IconChip> owns a record’s art, and a die face is not art: it is a number carrying marks. The simulator drew its faces on the 38px medallion until issue 2006; the tiles now own their geometry, and the four places a counted roll is read share one model rather than four derivations of which marks a die carries.
Shipped. Issue 2006 task 6 shipped the component, the model and the chat renderer and converted the Checks Studio simulator; the entry was measured against its specimen and flipped to shipped at issue 2461 (maintainer, 2026-10-12). The family sits once in styles/fabricate-chat-dialogs.css, which chat cards need because they render outside every Fabricate window, and is drawn by the result box, the salvage roll summary and both chat cards. The chat cards mix their tile tones against the chat message’s own ink (color-mix with currentcolor under .fabricate-craft-chat) where the app draws app tokens, so the chat unit here is drawn in app tokens as a stand-in.
09

Surfaces

Four ways of telling the reader something, and the rule that separates them.

<Callout> <Notice> <InfoStrip> <Empty>

Callout · shippedNotice · shippedInfoStrip · shippedEmpty · shipped
Notice evidence API (issue 1648). Optional evidence() snippet beneath the detail, with an 8px top margin and gap, 11px mono secondary ink. It carries bounded recorded check/receipt evidence belonging to this notice, never arbitrary page content. The default is absent. JournalFactRow's opt-in inline form composes compact This run facts using the existing .k-fact atom: muted label, adjacent 13px/500 mono value. Historical closed guidance uses the untitled neutral Callout.
callout — explains a rule that is always true, and stays put
Time only — nothing is awarded when this activity resolves. Reach for the info tint only when the note is about live state.
notice — reports something that just happened, or is wrong right now
This recipe cannot be saved
Step 2 has no ingredients, and the Critical result set routes to a tier that no longer exists.
Unsaved changes
Depth was raised to Full market. Prices start moving on the next tick.
4 essences deleted · 2 kept, still in use
One blocking bar at a time — danger owns the page. Non-blocking notices stack beneath it.
info strip — states current values, read-only, mono numerals
Crafting checkRequired
DC 151d20 + 34 h
The mono numerals are the tell — a strip is where a GM checks a figure without opening anything. No control ever lives in a strip.
empty — says what the emptiness means
No businesses yet
Businesses produce and consume goods. Add one and it becomes available to every settlement on this template.
No recipes match “ingot” in this system.
filtered is a real prop: “no results for this filter” and “nothing exists yet” are different sentences with different actions.
compact — a 32 tile and tighter padding, for a sidebar or a slot
No travel actor
Pick the actor that represents this party on the map.
inline — one line, the tile released into a bare glyph
Nothing goes wrong with this component yet. Add a complication to give a missed, partial or unlucky stage a consequence.
note — the popover line, with no panel
No actor matches your search.
field — inline at the width of a control, 34px high (issue 1649)
Add a weather condition
Any Weather
field sizes a short placeholder to the full control width at 34px, padded --fab-space-1 by --fab-space-2, beneath an availability dropdown.
fill — the whole box of a bounded host (issue 1648)
No completed runs yet.
fill stretches the border box to a bounded host’s whole width and height with no minimum height; journal list bodies use compact fill.
The routing rule
  • Callout — documentation. Always true, stays put.
  • Notice — state. Just happened, goes away.
  • InfoStrip — current values. Read-only facts in mono.
  • Empty — nothing to show, and why.
Callout API
  • SHIPPED — read from Callout.svelte’s $props() at issue 1505, when it was widened onto the geometry above and 12 importing files were re-authored against the tone rule this entry states, with three more becoming importers. Three further importers arrived with issue 1371 beneath this change; each already passed an explicit tone, and two carry that recorded judgement unchanged, while the salvage roll-budget note took a thirteenth re-authoring — info to neutral, matching the recipe editor’s twin of the same standing rule.
  • tone neutral | info | accent | warning | success | danger — neutral is the DEFAULT, which is the geometry above: the surface fill, the ordinary border, and the glyph carrying no colour of its own. The info tint is opt-in, reached only when the note is about live state. An unrecognised value falls back to neutral. At every TINTED tone the glyph takes the same --fab-<tone>-text as the title, mirroring the notice beside it, and at accent that ink is --fab-accent-text for the notice’s reason.
  • title — optional, and it borrows the NOTICE title’s treatment whole: 12px / 600, --fab-text at neutral and the tone’s own --fab-<tone>-text at every tinted tone, because a tinted box whose headline is the same grey in every state throws the ramp away. With a title present the body takes the notice detail’s own margin-top: 2px.
  • text — the sentence, which may be omitted when items carry the body; without it no body line renders. This component takes NO children snippet: every other shipped call site passes one localized string, and a snippet nothing renders is the unreachable configuration this reference exists to prevent.
  • icon — overrides the per-tone default glyph · actions a snippet, rendered inside the body, which is what lets a caller nest the control that used to sit beside the callout as a sibling.
  • items [{icon, lead, text}] — glyph-led points listed --fab-space-2 under the body (issue 1521, which folded the explainer card onto this entry). Each is a 13px glyph box inked like the leading glyph at every tone, a lead in --fab-text at 600, and its muted text. All three are optional and each renders only when non-empty, so an item with no icon releases the glyph column.
  • class an extra class, appended to the root’s own, plus a rest spread on the root — it carries the data-* hook a harness or a capture step selects on, and unlike the two components shipped beside it the hook is written bare on the tag, so it renders data-x="true" rather than data-x=""; nothing reads these values.
  • TARGET — none. There is no quiet prop: the geometry above IS the default now, so a caller opts into a tint rather than out of one. The root is a <p> for the plain form and a <div role="note"> when a title, actions or items are present, because a <p> cannot legally contain any of them.
Notice API
  • SHIPPED — this list was the SPECIFICATION and is now read from components/Notice.svelte’s $props() at issue 1505, with the eight deviations below.
  • tone danger | warning | info | success | accent — defaults to danger, which is the unmodified .k-notice above, and an unrecognised value falls back to it rather than rendering unstyled. accent is a recorded deviation from this list: the bulk report derives it for the destroy run and for the mixed outcome, and three published frames draw those states. At every tone the GLYPH and the TITLE take the same ink, which is the one rule the geometry above sets per tone; at accent, which this page declares no notice for, that ink is --fab-accent-text and never --fab-accent, because inking an accent band with the accent itself measures 4.48:1 in ironblood-forge.
  • title · detail — detail says what to do next, and it breaks at its newlines (white-space: pre-line), so a failure that joins several messages draws one per line (issue 2626). Recorded deviation: the detail carries tabular-nums, which the geometry above omits, over a live count sentence that resolves as a run completes.
  • icon — overrides the per-tone default glyph. Recorded deviation, and load-bearing: the bulk report resolves a destroy and a mixed outcome to the SAME accent tone with two different glyphs, so no per-tone default can express them.
  • action {label, onClick, description?} — an action with no non-blank string label, or with no function to call, draws no button · onAction, a top-level callback used when action.onClick is absent: recorded deviation (issue 2452) · recorded deviation (issue 2452): the action button is the default role at every tone, where the danger specimen above draws the danger role · recorded deviation (issue 2006): an already-localized description becomes the button’s accessible description, for an action whose verb alone does not state its effect · recorded deviation (issue 1773): the body takes a 12rem basis capped at its own text, so in a narrow host the action wraps beneath the body, at the trailing edge, instead of crushing it, while a wide notice and a short shrink-wrapped one keep one row · dismissable · dismissLabel — every button it emits carries data-keyboard-focus="true", and no label defaults to English text. dismissLabel is REQUIRED whenever dismissable is true: the dismiss control’s only visible content is a glyph, and spec.md requirement "Naming, announcement and hit targets are component obligations" and its scenario A primitive renders an icon-only control make an icon-only control’s accessible name a required prop rather than an optional one. It is written with an empty-string default and bound aria-label={dismissLabel || undefined} only so that an unset label OMITS the attribute, because an EMPTY aria-label suppresses the name instead of falling back to the content.
  • blocking boolean — a blocking notice replaces; the rest stack. It is what drives the announcement: role="alert" when blocking, and role="status" with aria-live="polite" otherwise — the ROLE carries it, because a live region created in the same mutation as its content is not announced and both shipped callers insert this component together with its text. The page-level arbitration is NOT claimed as met — the shared region that enforces one blocking notice per page is issue 1517’s, and a page still owes it until that region ships.
  • a rest spread on the root — the fourth recorded deviation, because this page has no test harness to enumerate hooks for. Attribute-only, carrying no behaviour; one spread carries every hook, because the alchemy banner carries two on one root, and a bare hook is written with an empty-string value so it renders data-x="" exactly as it did hand-rolled.
  • Announced through a live region when it appears without a focus change
InfoStrip API
  • SHIPPED — read from components/InfoStrip.svelte’s $props() at issue 1521, which built it on the census at the foot of this entry: the crafting check card and the gathering detail’s stamina pool are its two importers.
  • Props: label the optional kicker at the head of the strip, already localized · badge {label, tone}, a read-only state beside it drawn through the chip primitive in its own tone, which is how the worked example says the check is required · facts [{icon, label?, value, props}], an ordered list, each a decorative glyph, an optional body-type label, a caller-formatted mono value, and props spread on the fact for its hook and its title. Caller-formatted is the contract: a strip is where a GM checks a figure, so the figure arrives already stated and no arithmetic happens here. There is no tone: the strip is never tinted, so a state is its badge’s, and a fault is a danger notice after the strip.
  • Long values and reading order: a value is a caller-formatted figure, set in mono; a sentence-like value wraps in mono, and there is no per-fact type option to change that. Facts are read in order, each carrying its own label text, so they are bare inline facts rather than a list.
  • Passthrough: class plus a rest spread on the root, written after the class — the spread carries the data-* hook a harness or a capture step selects on, so the attribute is genuinely absent when unset.
  • Event contract: none, and that is the rule rather than an omission — no control ever lives in a strip, so a callback here would admit one. A facts list that needs an action belongs in a card.
  • Accessible naming: a group with exactly one name: its own kicker when one is drawn, otherwise ariaLabelledBy, otherwise ariaLabel, and a caller passes one of the three. Each fact’s glyph is decorative and the value carries the reading as text, which is what makes the mono numerals legible without colour. The strip is read-only, so nothing in it is focusable and it declares no focus pair.
  • Geometry — the third unit above: radius 9, --fab-space-3 padding, the --fab-bg-1 fill on the ordinary border, the facts wrapping --fab-space-2 by --fab-space-5 apart under the head, and each value 13px mono at 500 in --fab-text. Two figures are adjusted rather than taken: the glyph-to-value gap is --fab-space-chip for the specimen’s 7px, and a fact label inks --fab-text-muted rather than the glyph’s subtle ink, on the small-text contrast reading the eyebrow records.
Empty API
  • SHIPPED — read from EmptyState.svelte’s $props() at dd1eae56, the app’s one no-state panel. Its caller census lives on the manifest row rather than here, so the two cannot state different figures.
  • icon string, default '' — the glyph classes for the rounded tile; omitted, the panel renders without a tile, which is the second example above · title string, default '' — the short statement of what is absent, rendered as a heading inside the stack · hint string, default '' — the explanatory sentence, capped so it reads as a sentence rather than a paragraph.
  • filtered boolean, default false — “your filters match nothing”, which is a different sentence with a different action from “nothing exists yet”, and is the second panel drawn above: the specimen’s plain panel in the muted ink, on the hero’s edge, radius and padding, that deliberately skips the icon-and-title apparatus while keeping the one dashed vocabulary. 9 shipped sites.
  • compact boolean, default false, a 32px tile and tighter padding for a sidebar or a popover — a variant flag beside the four that follow, not a density value · inline boolean, default false, the one-line form, where the stack becomes a row and the tile is released into a bare glyph · note boolean, default false, the popover form, which releases the panel itself — no edge, no corner, no fill and no tile, one quiet line reading from the left at the popover’s own scale. note declares its own start alignment, so a caller cannot restore a centred line through a wrapper.
  • field boolean, default false, sizing a short placeholder to the full control width at 34px so it stands in for a control · fill boolean, default false, stretching the border box to a bounded host’s whole width and height with no minimum height, which puts the allocation in the caller’s hands rather than in the content’s.
  • contextClass string, default '' — extra classes describing how a container PLACES this panel, never how it looks; an appearance change is a prop here instead · a rest spread on the root, carrying the data-* hook a harness or a capture step selects on, so an unset hook is genuinely absent, and a bare hook renders ="true" · children the way out of the dead end — a recovery button, a primary action or a docs link — rendered INSIDE the panel, because a way out beside the panel reads as unrelated.
  • Event contract: none. It emits no control of its own; every action arrives as children and keeps its caller’s handler.
  • Accessible naming: none of its own, and deliberately so — it is not a landmark and it announces nothing. The title renders as a heading, the hint as a paragraph and the glyph is decorative, so the panel’s meaning is its text; the caller’s own button carries its own name.
  • TARGET — none. Every form is a drawn unit of this entry (issue 2550): the hero panel pads --fab-space-4 on a 1px --fab-border-strong dash, and filtered, compact, inline, note, field and fill each draw their own geometry. The DOM shape is part of the contract as it ships: the glyph, title and body rules are written as descendants of an inner stack, so flattening the wrapper silently drops the tile and the gap. One figure of the reference is corrected rather than taken — every variant inks its hint, and note its title, --fab-text-muted, because the subtle and disabled tones composite to 3.69:1 and 2.66:1 on the default theme’s surface at 10px to 11.5px, and the subtle tone falls under 4.5:1 in six of seven palettes (issue 2178). The muted ink clears 4.5:1 on --fab-bg-0, --fab-bg-1, --fab-surface, --fab-bg-2 and --fab-surface-soft over --fab-bg-2 in every palette, 4.60:1 at its weakest, in foundry-native on the soft ground. Issue 1710 promoted it out of the manager’s directory into components/.

A collapsed row disclosure is not the card primitive: it carries aria-expanded/aria-controls, and the chevron is a 24×24 radius-6 --fab-text-muted control beside the row’s content rather than the row itself. Its BODY is RULED in section 16: every row the shared ordered list renders keeps it in the DOM under display:none.
Card API
  • SHIPPED — read from InspectorCard.svelte’s $props() at issue 2315, at 38 importing files: 36 components render 88 tags, 17 of them flush, and the two published-component modules import it. It was extracted from 80 hand-written card sections across 20 components, and draws both card units above: radius 11, padding --fab-space-4, a 1px --fab-border edge on --fab-bg-2.
  • flush boolean, default false — padding 0, for a card whose head and body inset themselves, the second unit above. It emits is-flush and is unpublished: the published card takes children alone.
  • children snippet, default undefined — the body, as a snippet and not a head-and-body pair: a card is a container and has no fixed internal vocabulary to slot.
  • class string, default '' — an EXTRA class, appended after the primitive’s own and never replacing it. Every modifier other than flush travels this way, and a caller rule it keys places the card without restating its box.
  • Rest spread — written after the class, landing on the element it renders, and carrying every data-* hook, id and aria-label a call site had before the extraction. A bare data-* on a component tag is spelled with an empty string.
  • Event contract: none. It renders a non-interactive section and owns no control, which is also why it declares neither a font floor nor a focus pair: chrome declared here would displace an area’s chrome for a control this primitive does not own.
  • Accessible naming: none of its own and no role — a caller that needs the box named passes the name through the rest spread. A census walking each converted component’s tree found ONE host element, so it takes no polymorphism prop.
Well API
  • SHIPPED — drawn in the third unit above and as the collapsible card’s body in the second, and built at issue 2008 as components/Well.svelte, read here from its $props(); its props and geometry are this specimen’s. It is the only level below <Card>: a third container is not in this vocabulary. Two independent callers draw it: the Checks Studio’s option group and the roll prompt’s additional-dice control, which takes this fill where the prototype paints that well a step lighter.
  • Props: label the optional kicker at its head, which is what the specimen draws · children the body · class an EXTRA class, appended after the primitive’s own fab-well, on the card’s own terms. It takes no radius, padding or fill prop: one nested level means one geometry — a 1px --fab-border frame, radius 9 and --fab-space-3 padding on --fab-bg-1 — and a well that could be re-shaped by a caller would be the drift this pair exists to end.
  • Rest spread — written last on the element it renders, carrying every data-* hook, id, role and aria-*, as the card’s does. A bare data-* on a component tag is spelled with an empty string.
  • Event contract: none. A well is a container; the control that opens or closes the card around it belongs to that card.
  • Accessible naming: named by its kicker where it has one, as a group carrying the kicker’s words, and it renders a plain element rather than a section, so nesting one inside a card adds no landmark a reader has to walk past. A caller naming it otherwise passes the role and name through the rest spread, which wins.
RowDisclosure API
  • SHIPPED — read from RowDisclosure.svelte’s $props() at issue 1512, which promoted it on a second independent importer: SortableList renders it as the sole opener of every ordered row. The props below are the component’s, not the specimen’s draft of them — the earlier summary / children / density set was authored from the unit above and shipped props are the specification.
  • Props: expanded · controls the id of the region this discloses, required for aria-controls to mean anything · ariaLabel the accessible name · side trailing or leading, which decides only which way the collapsed chevron points · disabled.
  • Passthrough: class plus a rest spread on the root, written after the class — the spread carries the data-* hook a harness or a capture step selects on, so the attribute is genuinely absent when unset.
  • Event contract: onToggle receives the new expanded state, and the caller owns expanded. The CHEVRON is the control and it sits BESIDE the row’s content: it renders a real <button>, so a whole-row button around it would nest buttons, which is invalid DOM that createElement accepts and no mounted test notices. That is ONE of the two shapes the ordered-row requirement rules; where the opener is the WHOLE HEADER the header is itself the button, cannot nest this component, and names itself from its own content plus a visually hidden phrase, which section 16 carries as a RULED row.
  • Accessible naming: the chevron is a button carrying the expanded state and pointing at the body it controls, named for the ROW it opens rather than for the action, because aria-expanded supplies the rest. The name is emitted only when non-empty, since aria-label="" is a label of nothing rather than no label, and it declares data-keyboard-focus="true". A closed row’s body is RULED in section 16 — kept in the DOM wherever the shared ordered list renders it — so no prop here settles it either.
The card ships as InspectorCard.svelte and draws this specimen. Issue 2315, measured with this commit. It was extracted from 80 hand-written class="manager-inspector-card" sections (a class issue 1507 retired) across 20 components, all of them a <section>, and 36 components now render it 88 times. Geometry: radius 11, padding --fab-space-4, a 1px --fab-border edge and --fab-bg-2, the first unit above. Variant: flush draws padding 0, the second unit, for the 17 cards whose head and body inset themselves: the Checks Studio’s cards, the Checks rail’s two lists and the systems card on a world entry. Callers place it: a caller rule sets margin, flex or grid placement, gap or position and never restates padding, fill, radius or border, and a status tone — border-color and a --fab-*-soft fill from one status ramp — is not a restatement. The Tools and Essences inspectors paint no pane-sized card, the Checks rail’s cards moved from --fab-bg-1 to --fab-bg-2, and a card never contains a card. <Well>, the level below it, shipped at issue 2008 as Well.svelte.InspectorCard.svelte — 36 rendering components · ui-visual-style/spec.md · card-drawing-parity.test.js
The card is now rooted at the class the primitive emits, and it declares NEITHER a floor nor a focus pair. Issue 1508, measured with this commit, and about the Card name in this heading only. InspectorCard.svelte writes fabricate-card as the first literal of its own class array, and both of the two selectors the gate judges owned — the flex stack and the box — are compounds on that root instead of .fabricate-manager. The Checks Studio’s .manager-checks-card override is a caller-CLASS compound and carries the root too, because leaving it behind would have split the rule; since issue 2315 it only places the card (gap 0, overflow hidden) and its box is the shared card’s. No rule naming a caller’s own rail or inspector remains. The absence of chrome is the recorded decision, not an omission. This primitive renders a <section> and owns no control of its own, so a floor or a ring declared here would displace an area’s chrome for a control the primitive does not own. A negative control asserts that no rule under this root declares either half. The box’s radius and fill moved onto the specimen’s at issue 1523. The tab-bar family is now rooted at the class the primitive emits, and the gate reads a class a component declares as a PROP DEFAULT. Issue 1509, measured with this commit. The shipped strip writes that class at the head of its own role="tablist" element, and reads its three vocabulary classes out of a frozen map so the gate can see them as emission: they were $props() DEFAULTS, which no reader saw, and eleven of the family’s thirteen selectors would otherwise have stayed app-rooted with the gate reporting the family clean. Seven owned selectors and one caller-CLASS compound were re-rooted and one selector list was SPLIT; five that name a caller’s own column, panel or per-site vocabulary stayed app-rooted and exempt at that commit. It is the ONE family in that change that owns a control of its own — the <button role="tab"> it renders — so it is the one that declares chrome: a font: inherit floor at .fabricate-tabs button, (0,1,1), joining the shared group below the area baseline, and a NEW focus pair with the strip written immediately above the repaint. The strip’s own type is (0,2,0) and out-ranks the floor.EditorTabs.svelte · fabricate.css .fabricate-tabs button, .fabricate-tabs button:focus, .fabricate-tabs button:focus-visible
The tab bar draws the Rail Marker Family, and it is a capability rather than a per-strip choice. The player application’s two hand-rolled strips render the tab bar. Issue 1518 moved gathering/GatheringDetailTabs.svelte and the Info | Salvage strip in inventory/InventoryComponentDetail.svelte onto EditorTabs.svelte, a real tablist with arrow-key selection, and the adoption walk covers the five player directories with no player host on its allow-list.
One family rule draws the tab, and the chip draws its issue badge, at issue 2464. The sheet’s strip, tab, hover and current-tab rules each name both class vocabularies in one selector list, manager-editor-* and manager-environment-*, and the four drawings that stood beside them are deleted: the manager-environment-* alias, the Checks section strip, the component-entry strip and the tool strip’s 832–900px rung.
