The arrangement is fixed
  • verdict icon chip + serif line + one sentence — the answer before the evidence
  • counts pass, warn, blocking, always all three, always in that order
  • groups kickered by the part of the record, in the order the editor's own tabs run
  • issue severity glyph, title, one sentence, and a Fix that moves focus to the offending control
  • Full width, no inspector rail — the issues are the content
Rules
  • A passing group still renders, so a GM can see what was checked rather than infer it from silence
  • Blocking always sorts above warning inside a group
  • The verdict states what the blocking issues prevent, in the product's words, not "1 error"
  • The same component renders this on every editor — recipe, essence, tool, check
Why it is a screen and not a panel. Validation is where a GM goes when something is wrong, which is the worst moment to make them learn a new layout. Three editors ship it today with three arrangements; one arrangement everywhere is worth more than any per-editor tailoring.EditorValidationSurface.svelte · checks, essence and tool validation tabs

15

Ruled out

Candidates reviewed and declined. Each is a composition of parts already in the set, one-screen furniture, a surface Foundry already owns, or a second name merged into an entry that already exists. Kept so the reasoning survives and nobody re-proposes them.

Out<MemberRow>

List row geometry with a portrait in the leading cell — structurally identical to the inline-title row already declined. Compose: ListRow + leading.

Out<ActorPicker>

A pill trigger that opens the popover — which already counted it as one of its four callers. Compose: trigger + SearchPopover.

Out<AddButton>

Dashed is a role on the button that owns the meaning. “Sits in flow with its collection” is a usage rule, not a boundary. Compose: Button role=dashed.

Out<RailCard>

A composition that also smuggled back the 34px button size the set retires by name. Compose: Well + Kicker + Button.

Out<FeatureCard>

Two absent props on an identical shape is a props difference, not a distinction. Compose: OptionCards, non-interactive.

Out<PremiumPanel>

A screen, not a primitive. Its one original claim is copy — a product decision — and binding copy to a component makes the offer untranslatable. Canon also forbids any premium signal in the player window.

Out<BoundsInput>

“Two steppers with a rule between”, by its own spec. Compose: two Steppers.

Out<CurrencyInput>

A composition, and wrong about the domain: it assumed a flat world-scoped coin ladder where the model defines a per-system acyclic denomination DAG. Compose: Stepper + Select.

OutControl caption

A one-line sentence DOCUMENTING THE CONTROL DIRECTLY ABOVE IT, and it is neither a callout nor a mark. The deciding question is whether the sentence is a statement about the WORLD or a caption for a CONTROL: <Callout> owns the standing statement, which stays true whether or not anything is drawn beside it, while a caption says nothing about the world and dies with its control. Measured at the gathering tab’s event-chance hint (issue 1514): routed through <Callout> the line rendered 432.3×44.39 against the 432.3×15 its bare <p> draws — a border, a soft fill, an r11 corner and a 12px inset wrapped around a caption for the 6px track above it. Stays a bare line until a second independent caller justifies naming the shape.

Out<Toast>

Foundry owns transient feedback and renders its own toasts over the module window regardless. Use: ui.notifications.

OutDestructive panel

Canon makes the dialog the default for manager confirmations; the arm is the carve-out. Use: confirmDialog.

Merged<ValidationList>

The grouped row list is the same tab as the verdict above it, drawn by the one shipped surface, so a second name would have pointed at no implementation of its own. Merged by maintainer ruling 4 (2026-09-18): “One component, merge the entries.” Use: <ValidationSummary>.

Merged<AppRail>

The player window’s icon rail and the manager’s sidebar are one component with a variant: they share the item model and the active treatment, so a second name would have pointed at the same file. Merged by issue 1777 decision E2. Use: <NavSidebar>, variant icon.

Merged<BrowseCard>

The card grid is the same row model on one track, so a second name would have pointed at the row’s own file. Merged by issue 1778 decision D2. Use: <ListRow>, layout="card".

CompositionFive more

Inline-title row, thumbnail tile, full-width CTA, locked preview list, studio footer bar. The thumbnail tile is art on IconChip and the CTA is fullWidth on Button, so both are expressible without a component.

Zero callersGraph canvas

No Svelte consumer: the dependency graph is a disabled placeholder behind an experimental flag. It re-enters the set with the work that ships it.

This list is the set of KNOWN debts rather than a proof of conformance elsewhere — an absence here means nobody has checked, not that a surface conforms. It also carries the debts this reference owes itself: a name used here with no entry behind it.

Derived from a review of 21 prototypes against the shipped app, covering set boundaries, behavioural completeness and Foundry integration.
Sources: 21 prototype bundles, the shipped Svelte app under src/ui/, openspec/specs/ui-integration/spec.md, DOMAIN.md, AGENTS.md, styles/fabricate.css, lang/en.json, and the harvested Foundry client.
Every specimen on this page is rendered from the same token values the app ships, at the geometry each entry specifies. Single-theme by intent — all seven shipped themes are dark.
